1 · Executive Summary

OSS Insights answers a question SBOMs can't: not "what open-source software do we have installed?" but "should we be concerned about what we have?" Every application depends on hundreds of open-source projects, each with its own community, release cadence, and lifecycle. A package with zero known vulnerabilities can still be a serious and growing risk — if the project behind it is end-of-life, abandoned, or years behind on releases, nobody is coming to fix the next vulnerability. Today, no scanner surfaces that. OSS Insights attaches upstream project health to every package Anchore already tracks, turning inventory into a forward-looking risk assessment.

4 new builds · 5 extensions of existing services · scope decision 2026-07-16: package EOL is the active effort; the distro view is retained for comparison

What users will get

The first release puts a lifecycle status on every package in an application version — Active, End-of-Life, or Does-Not-Exist — visible as a badge in the package listing, as a rollup metric on the version summary, as a filter ("show me every EOL dependency"), and as a policy rule that can gate a build the same way vulnerability policies do. From there the same machinery grows into the full health picture: maintenance activity, release currency ("how many versions behind are we?"), historical responsiveness to security disclosures, and a per-package health panel — the direction the product designs already lay out.

The moving parts

Nine components make this work — most of them extensions of machinery Anchore already runs in production for vulnerability data, four of them genuinely new:

ComponentJobBasis
Collection pipelineContinuously gathers per-project health facts (lifecycle status, release history, activity) from public sourcesnew working prototype, validated at ~99% coverage / ~96% accuracy against ground truth
Health datasetThe product of collection: a versioned database with one health record per open-source projectnew
DistributionPublishes the dataset to customer deployments on a scheduleextend the same service that ships the vulnerability DB today
License checkMakes insights a purchasable add-on: only entitled licenses can download the datasetextend existing licensing, new per-dataset granularity
Dataset syncPulls the dataset into the deployment — including the existing offline bundle for air-gapped sitesextend existing feed sync, new dataset type
Platform integrationLoads each dataset update and attaches health records to the customer's packages, keeping them current as data refreshesextend the proven vulnerability feed-update machinery
Product APIsExpose health on every package: per-package detail, version-level summaries, filtersextend existing package APIs
User interfaceStatus badges, filters, rollup metrics, the package health panelnew designs complete (closed 2026-07-13)
Policy enginePolicy rules that gate builds on EOL or unhealthy dependencies — one generic gate keying off any insight, re-evaluated automatically when the dataset updatesnew gate on the existing policy framework; re-evaluation rides the proven feed-update machinery

Two properties hold across the whole system: customer package data never leaves the deployment — the dataset covers the open-source universe and all matching happens locally, so a fully air-gapped installation gets the complete feature; and new health metrics ship as data, flowing from collection to UI without customer software upgrades.

Status · after the 2026-07-16 engineering offsite
Engineering and product walked this document end to end and confirmed the component breakdown. Scope is locked to package-level EOL (distro EOL split into a separate effort); the collection pipeline carries ~80% of the work and all of the schedule risk; and the first milestone is agreed: an end-to-end pipeline publishing into the ADS dev account with two data pieces under separate license entitlements, demonstrating data appearing and disappearing through to the UI with zero code changes in between. Full outcomes: the offsite decisions document in the appendix, and the updated register and decision log.

2 · Product Context

The feature area is named "OSS Insights" in the internal concept doc (appendix, verbatim). EOL applies at two levels — the open-source packages inside an application, and the distribution the image is built on — and both are on the roadmap as separate deliverables on a shared pipeline. The product diagram attached to the initiative brands it "Insights Powered by Anchore AI."

Package EOL vs distro EOL

The two deliverables run the same pipeline end to end; they differ in the data and the join:

Package EOLDistro EOL
Datasetone record per open-source project; 100k–1M+ rowsone record per distro release line; roughly a thousand rows
Sourcemulti-source collection pipeline (new build)endoflife.date, already ingested by the existing vulnerability-data pipeline — with per-release EOL dates
Matchingcanonical package identity: purl normalization at universe scaledistro identity is already first-class in the platform; only a small name-mapping is needed
Surfacespackage rows, package filters, a packages policy gateasset/image level, asset views (UI design complete), an image policy gate

Everything between collection and surfacing — publishing, distribution, licensing, sync, and platform load — is the same shared machinery for both; whichever ships first builds it and the other inherits it.

Scope decision · offsite 2026-07-16
This effort is package EOL only. Distro EOL was explicitly split out: it joins at the asset/image level rather than package rows, an SBOM can legitimately contain multiple distros, and its raw data already ships inside the grype vulnerability DB (never copied into Postgres today). How and when to productize it is a separate decision.

Design intent (ENTERPRISE-8519)

Constraint · Zachary Hill on 6095
1. Data-driven insights: API shapes carry insights: [{metric, value}, …] keyed by purl — new insight datasets must ship without software upgrades. 2. Add-on SKUs: insight datasets are independently-toggleable add-ons; only technically-inseparable data may be bundled (then as one atomic add-on). Both constraints are satisfied structurally in the schema (section 6) and entitlement design (section 7).

5 · Deep Dive: Data Acquisition

Full analysis in the appendix ("Data-Acquisition Deep Dive", 748 lines, every claim cited). The two headlines: one coverage-critical source carries a share-alike license, and the universe is too large to crawl — acquisition must run on bulk snapshots and change feeds rather than per-package API calls.

The licensing landmine — sharpened by measurement
ecosyste.ms is the coverage backstop, the experiment corpus source, and the validation oracle — and its data is CC-BY-SA (viral share-alike). Either negotiate their commercial license or restructure so ecosyste.ms data never enters the shipped dataset. Measured update (2026-08-08): the hoped-for CC0 fallback is weaker than assumed — on a random 350-package universe sample, ClearlyDefined returned no data for 97–100% of packages in every ecosystem tested (it covers curated/popular packages, not the long tail). The clean-license spine is therefore deps.dev (CC-BY) + native registries + derived forge metrics; ClearlyDefined contributes license-clean corroboration only where it happens to have data, and the ecosyste.ms commercial-license question carries more weight than the original framing suggested.
The rate-limit math
14M packages at ecosyste.ms's paid 5,000 req/hr ≈ 117 days per full pass. Per-record REST crawling can only be the delta/verification tier. Primary acquisition: deps.dev BigQuery snapshots + registry dumps + ClearlyDefined hourly changesets; incremental updated-after queries where offered.

The vunnel precedent — what gets reused

vunnel (the grype vulnerability-data pipeline) already solves incremental acquisition: providers implement only name() + update(last_updated); the framework supplies workspace/state tracking, checksummed result stores (sqlite, atomic replace), schema-versioned records, retry-aware HTTP, and EDS orchestrates a per-provider dated S3 cache with warm restore. It even ships an eol provider (endoflife.date) already — proof that non-vuln payloads fit, and a head start for distro EOL.

Recommended shape: an insights-specific pipeline that lifts workspace.py / result.py / http_wrapper.py nearly verbatim, with bulk-ingest steps vunnel doesn't model; bounded sources become literal vunnel providers only where grype/EDS also wants them.

6 · Deep Dive: Dataset & Schema

Full DDL, query pseudocode, and cost analysis in the appendix ("Schema & Middleware Design"). This section carries the decisions and the reasoning.

Postgres (NG component_catalog) — three tables, all global

TableRoleKey design points
component_catalog_oss_projectsDataset mirrorKeyed by canonical version-less purl. Hybrid columns: typed status / eol / dne / latest_version + four time metrics (indexable, policy-facing) plus a verbatim metrics JSONB array — new dataset metrics reach the API with zero platform code change (the product constraint that new metrics ship without software upgrades). Each row carries a content hash, so a new dataset version is compared against the previous one with a single indexed join and the change set falls out of the load. The table is replaced wholesale on every dataset update.
component_catalog_package_insightsResolution table (the junction)At most one row per package, keyed by the package's primary key with a cascading foreign key — deleting a package deletes its resolution row with it. Holds resolved project link + materialized version_lag + bucket. Unmatched packages keep a row with normalized purl populated — new dataset projects re-resolve waiting packages via one partial index, no table scan.
component_catalog_oss_insights_db_stateBookkeeping singletonMirrors vulnerability_db_state: checksum debounce, dataset schema_version, metric registry.

Global (non-tenant) tables follow the existing EPSS/KEV precedent — account scoping stays at the asset/app-version join.

Why a resolution table beats a direct purl join

  1. The join can't use the index: NG's packages.base_purl contains the version; joining to version-less project purls needs an expression join — un-indexable at listing time.
  2. Normalization drift becomes permanent silent misses: current packageurl-python folds Django→django, typing_extensions→typing-extensions — but package rows written under older library versions are immutable. A write-time resolution step can be re-run; a read-time join cannot be fixed.
  3. Version lag must be materialized anyway: it's a per-(installed version × release list) computation — there has to be a row to hold the result.

Read cost: one PK LEFT JOIN per row — ~1–5 ms on a 5k-package listing.

One idempotent resolver, three triggers

resolve_insights_for_packages(scope) -> changed_package_ids
  # scope ∈ {package_ids} | {changed_purls} | ALL
  # 1. select target packages (by id, by normalized-purl match, or all non-sentinel)
  # 2. normalize purl → look up oss_projects → compute version_lag via ecosystem comparator
  # 3. UPSERT package_insights rows; skip no-ops; return truly-changed package_ids

triggers:
  SBOM ingest        → resolver(package_ids just stamped)      # same-job post-step, ~ms
  dataset refresh    → resolver(differ's changed purls)        # then events + policy fanout
  full re-resolve    → resolver(ALL)                           # dataset schema upgrades / normalization version bump

This answers the "one piece of code or two" question: one — initialization and maintenance are the same function invoked with different scopes, and its changed-ids return value is exactly what event/policy fanout consumes.

The database that ships over the wire

Near-mirror of the PG mirror table (meta + oss_projects with record_hash), loaded by a typed transform (not a blind copy) gated on MAJOR.MINOR schema_version: exactly one consumer justifies tight alignment; the version gate is what makes the coupling safe. The generic differ is LEFT JOIN old ON pk WHERE hash differs — the same contract the vulnerability layer meets with grype db diff.

Sizing calculator

1.0M
project rows
32M

1.3 GB
sqlite raw (est.)

Model: ~500 B/project row incl. indexes; zstd ≈ 5×. Two independent estimates — one from per-record byte budgets, one computed bottom-up from the proposed table schema — converge on 15 / 150 / 700 MB compressed at 100k / 1M / 5M projects. Recommendation: curated ≤1M universe with capped timelines → an artifact the same class as the vulnerability DB.

7 · Deep Dive: Delivery & Entitlements

How datasets reach customers today, verified in code across enterprise-data-service, -infra, anchore-lms, and enterprise v5 — and the decided entitlement design.

GH Actions cron (prod 6h / integ nightly) └▶ EDS dataset workflow: build → validate → publish ──▶ S3 archives + listing.json (grype-db · clamav · KEV · EPSS · STIG · match-exclusions · [oss-insights-db]) S3 ──▶ API Gateway + lambdas (authorizer → usage-plan key; get-listing / handle-dataset / schema-list) └▶ anchorectl airgap feed download --key … ──▶ feeds.tar (checksum-skip; airgap: same file, walked in) └▶ data_syncer drivers: store archive in object store + record → notify NG (/notify/*) └▶ internal datasets API: /v2/datasets/{name}/{version}/latest → every service, incl. NG

Access control today — thinner than it looks

  • The authorizer lambda validates nothing about the license: it regex-extracts Bearer v1_anc_{api_key} and defers to the API Gateway usage plan; policy is Allow on *.
  • The dataset lambdas have zero per-customer logic — every valid key gets every dataset. Proof of the gap: STIG profiles are a paid add-on entitlement, yet the archive is served to any valid key; the flag only gates the enterprise UI/API. Add-on data is honor-system today.
  • LMS provisioning: at license creation, if Third_Party_Feeds is among the entitlements, anchore-lms creates an API GW key, embeds it as data.apiKey, adds it to one global usage plan, and RSA-SHA256-signs the license details. One binary flag = master switch for all datasets. No revocation path exists; an expired license's key keeps working.
Verified against code 2026-08-07 · one correction
The flow above says "S3 archives + listing.json" — true for every dataset except the grype vulnerability DB v6, which uses a newer divergent pattern: databases/grype/v6/latest.json ({path, built, checksum}) with pre-signed URLs, special-cased in the download handler. There are therefore two serving patterns in production, and the insights dataset must pick one deliberately — the listing.json shape is what a KEV-template workflow produces for free; latest.json+presign is the newer direction. The handler also branches on private-API-gateway presigning; new dataset serving inherits both branches. (Register row below; verification by the data-feeds pillar session, which also confirmed the authorizer, entitlement-absence, and checksum-skip claims in this section against current main.)

The decided design — stateless license-in-request

Decision · operator · 2026-07-13
The client sends the full signed license with each request; the lambda verifies the RSA signature against a list of trusted public keys, checks the validity window, cross-checks license.data.apiKey == the presented bearer key, and reads entitlements directly. No backend entitlement database — no synchronization problem, significantly less code; the few-KB/request cost is insignificant. Bonus: per-request expiry checking fixes the expired-key hole with zero key-lifecycle plumbing.
Hardening detailWhy
Keep the API GW usage-plan key underneathMid-term revocation brake (churn, leaked license) + rate limiting + existing usage metrics
license.data.apiKey == bearer key cross-checkPrevents pairing a leaked entitled license with a different valid key
Validate in the dataset lambdas, not the authorizerAvoids API GW authorizer-cache/policy-scope complexity; license travels in a custom header (b64) or body
Trust a list of public keysSigning-key rollover without breaking deployed customers

Migration is backward-compatible: key-only clients keep base datasets; flag-gated datasets require the license-bearing client. Entitlement changes need no proactive handling — the next sync cycle downloads newly-entitled datasets naturally. LMS change: add the insights entitlement option(s) to the menu (naming/bundling is an open product decision). Enterprise change: extend LicenseEntitlement / Features / FeatureMap. Usage-tracking records gain a dataset dimension.

8 · Deep Dive: Platform Integration (NG)

The vulnerability feed-update workflow is the template. Verified push chain: data_syncer's driver calls notify_feed_update() → NG POST /notify/feed-update → create_workflow(FEED_UPDATE) immediately. (ensure_ready is the pre-scan gate and multi-container convergence/safety net — not the trigger.)

The vulnerability workflow (today)

notify ──▶ FEED_UPDATE workflow (4 steps) 1 diff download new sqlite (object store), `grype db diff` old↔new — STREAMED into a paused rescan queue 2 rescan scan units resolved via 4 query paths; change-set derived from the write path itself 3 events change-sets → app hierarchy (scan_started_at fence) → one ApplicationVulnsUpdated per app 4 policy placeholder PENDING rows (API shows "stale" immediately) + one re-eval job per app-version

The generalization: metadata layers

Most of this machinery is already dataset-agnostic: the data syncer's dataset registry and internal serving API, the job framework's workflows, work queues, and drain handlers, the translation from changed package identities to affected application versions, and the policy re-evaluation queue all work unchanged for any dataset. A new dataset type implements five functions; everything else is shared:

layer = {
  dataset_name, schema_version,
  loader(archive)      -> PG tables, atomic swap (insights: DELETE+INSERT in one transaction)
  differ(old, new)     -> stream[identity_key]   (insights: generic hash differ; vulns keep grype db diff)
  translator(keys, ts) -> {(account, app_id): [version_ids]}   (insights: purl-keyed variant)
  event_factory(...)   -> per-app event (+ v5 stub + notifications formatter)
  policy_relevant      -> gates the stale-policy step (needs the new packages policy gate)
}
FEED_UPDATE  ⟶  METADATA_UPDATE(layer): notify → load+diff → [recompute iff layer needs it] → translate → events → policy
The key simplification
Vulnerabilities must re-match after a feed lands (expensive: grype, scanner pool, validation modes). Insights need no recompute step at all — new metadata replaces old, so "what changed" is the diff, and the diff keys feed straight into the resolver → translation → events. The hard parts of the vuln pipeline are exactly the parts insights doesn't need.

Full load flow for the insights layer: data_syncer notify → loader swaps oss_projects in one transaction → differ emits changed purls → resolve_insights_for_packages(changed_purls) → truly-changed package ids → app-version translation → events + stale-policy queue (once a packages policy gate exists to re-evaluate). Rollback = re-load the prior archive from the data syncer's retained records + full re-resolve.

UI feasibility · verified live in the on-prem UI 2026-08-07
The UI pillar session booted the on-prem UI in-container and verified the demo surface: the Contents tab already runs on a declarative table stack (typed Filter descriptors), so a new status column + filter is ~10 small, enumerated edits; an unreferenced lifecycle-status component already exists in-tree; entitlement gating is native (routes/nav vanish when a feature flag is absent — the Milestone-1 on/off beat, with one caveat: entitlements load once at boot, so the demo's disappear/reappear step includes a UI-server restart); and data-driven rendering precedent exists — the reports view builds filters/columns from an introspected schema and the policy editor renders forms from a runtime-fetched spec, so schema-advertised insights columns are established pattern, not novel architecture. New entitlements/fields enter via the swagger spec + codegen, not hand-written types.

Every design decision made during this effort, with rationale and rejected alternatives. D1 and D14–D15 are operator decisions; the rest are analysis conclusions adopted into the design (overridable).

D1Stateless license-in-request entitlement
Send the full signed license with each dataset request; lambda verifies RSA signature (public-key list), validity window, and apiKey↔bearer cross-check; reads entitlements directly. API GW usage-plan key retained as revocation brake.
No backend entitlement DB = no synchronization problem, less code/state; per-request expiry check fixes the expired-key hole for free. Rejected: DynamoDB entitlement registry (state to sync); authorizer-side validation (cache-key complexity).operator, 2026-07-13
D2Resolution table over direct purl join
One optional resolution row per package (component_catalog_package_insights, keyed by the package primary key) connects packages to their project health records.
base_purl contains the version (un-indexable expression join); normalization drift on immutable rows becomes permanent misses; version lag must be materialized somewhere regardless.schema analysis
D3One shared idempotent resolver
resolve_insights_for_packages(package_ids | changed_purls | ALL) serves SBOM ingest, dataset refresh, and full re-resolve.
Initialization and maintenance are the same operation with different scopes; returns truly-changed ids for event fanout. Answers 'one piece of code or two': one.schema analysis
D4Near-mirror sqlite + typed transform loader
Wire sqlite mirrors the PG mirror table; loader is a typed transform gated on MAJOR.MINOR schema_version — not a blind copy.
One consumer justifies tight alignment; the version gate makes the coupling safe; typed transform catches drift at load, not at query.schema analysis
D5Generalize FEED_UPDATE to METADATA_UPDATE(layer)
Layer interface: loader / differ / translator / event_factory / policy_relevant. Vuln layer keeps grype-diff+rescan; insights uses generic hash differ, no recompute.
The data syncer, job framework, hierarchy translation, and policy re-evaluation queue are already dataset-agnostic; a third dataset becomes an interface implementation with zero new plumbing.feed-update analysis
D6DELETE+INSERT single-transaction dataset swap
Loader replaces oss_projects wholesale in one tx (existing reader-compat precedent).
Simplest atomic swap at these row counts; partition/rename machinery unjustified.schema analysis
D7No recompute step for insights
The diff IS the change-set; changed purls feed the resolver directly.
Insights metadata replaces rather than re-matches; grype-style rescan machinery not needed.feed-update analysis
D8Query-time summary rollups
GROUPING SETS over status + lag bucket at request time; no precomputed aggregates.
100–5k packages/version make query-time cheap; precompute adds a maintenance surface (no precomputed aggregate tables to maintain).schema analysis
D9Per-app events on dataset refresh
Same drain pattern as ApplicationVulnsUpdated: new event class + v5 stub + notifications formatter (matches the existing notification contract).
Consistency with the existing consumer contract; notifications delivery requires the v5 pair.feed-update analysis
D10[demoted to candidate] Insights inline on PackageResponse
status + lag first-class, metrics verbatim array — the schema analysis's recommendation.
DEMOTED 2026-08-07: the offsite transcript shows inline-vs-separate was explicitly deferred with the entitlement-absence constraint attached; this is a candidate awaiting the API design decision (register O14), not a made decision.schema analysis; demoted after transcript review
D11Reuse vunnel modules, not the framework wholesale
Lift workspace.py / result.py / http_wrapper.py into an insights-specific pipeline; literal vunnel providers only for bounded shared sources.
Universe-scale sources need bulk ingest vunnel doesn't model; avoids coupling insights cadence to the grype-db repo.data-sources analysis
D12Bulk-first acquisition
BigQuery snapshots + registry dumps + ClearlyDefined hourly changesets as primary; per-record REST only as delta/verification tier.
Rate-limit math: 14M packages ≈ 117 days/pass at 5k req/hr.data-sources analysis
D13Data-driven lambda dataset registry
Replace the triplicated if/elif with name → {{s3 prefix, listing, required_entitlement}}; schema-list filtered by entitlement.
New datasets become registry rows; dynamic discovery = add-ons appear without client upgrades.gap analysis
D14No proactive license-change handling
Entitlement changes materialize at the next sync cycle naturally.
'We don't want to write extra code if we don't have to' — the design gives this for free.operator, 2026-07-13
D15Local-only matching (privacy invariant)
The dataset covers the universe; all package matching happens inside the deployment; air-gapped installs run the full algorithm via feeds.tar.
Customer package data never leaves the deployment; sizing envelope (section 6) is the accepted cost.operator direction
D16Distro EOL descoped from this effort
Package EOL is the scope of this analysis and build; distro EOL is a separate use case (asset-level, different cardinality/schema/APIs) to be decided independently — its raw data already ships inside the grype DB.
Different join grain and surfaces; convolving them muddies both. Offsite 2026-07-16.offsite decision
D17Backend-generated universe, Syft-dialect purls
The package universe is generated server-side from public sources — vulnerability-known purls first, Syft-generated SBOMs over public container registries, then registry listings — never from customer data.
Purls are invented strings; harvesting our own cataloger's output aligns the dataset with customer SBOM purls and preserves the air-gap/privacy invariant. Offsite 2026-07-16.offsite decision
D18Cloud-native collection infrastructure
AWS managed services, long-running stateful orchestration, serverless-friendly, no self-managed VMs; existing SSO for internal tooling; low operational overhead is a hard requirement.
No engineer will be dedicated to babysitting this; cost premium for managed services is acceptable. Offsite 2026-07-16.offsite decision
D19Stage persistence with audit, validators, and a corrections path
Every pipeline stage persists output; per-record evidence/audit trails; validators run inside the pipeline at stage boundaries; a read-only inspection dashboard first, gaining write (centralized corrections) later.
Data-engineering correctness: errors caught at stage boundaries don't cascade; 'why is it this value' must be answerable from evidence. Offsite 2026-07-16 (pattern proposed by Zach, endorsed by Dan).offsite decision
D20Known-unknowns are first-class; nothing defaults
Missing data never defaults to a value (absence of EOL data ≠ active). Confident-vs-unknown is an explicit, surfaced distinction.
A wrong default is worse than an honest unknown, and for this data (unlike vulnerabilities) customers accept known-unknowns. Offsite 2026-07-16.offsite decision
D21Data-driven end to end: generic gate, schema-advertising API, dynamic UI
One generic policy gate keys off any insight key; APIs expose insights as schema-described key/value data; the UI renders columns/filters from the advertised schema.
Enables Neil's requirement: new insights reach existing deployments as data, no software upgrade. Offsite 2026-07-16.offsite decision
D22Enterprise annotations and overrides committed
Two layers: centralized corrections (true for everyone, shipped in the dataset) and deployment-local annotations/contextualization, mirroring vulnerability annotations.
Customers will have context we can't know (commercial backports); analysts must be able to dismiss findings with reasons. Offsite 2026-07-16.offsite decision
D23Store the dataset unpruned in each deployment
No inventory-based pruning; the full (entitled) dataset lives locally.
Keeps delta sync simple and makes arbitrary-purl lookup architecturally free; V1 sizes (~1GB) don't justify pruning complexity. Offsite 2026-07-16.offsite decision
D24Milestone 1: two-entitlement dynamism demo
End-to-end pipeline POC publishing into the ADS dev AWS account with two data pieces under separate entitlements: load a license → data appears through to the UI; remove it → it disappears; zero code changes in between.
Proves the entire data-driven delivery thesis before scale investment. Offsite 2026-07-16.offsite decision
D26Pipeline repo: anchore/insights-data-service
The collection pipeline gets a new private repo named insights-data-service, paralleling enterprise-data-service: EDS delivers datasets, IDS produces them.
Names the producer/deliverer pair legibly; private per the proprietary-dataset decision.operator, 2026-08-07
D27Prototype the pipeline locally before choosing operational infrastructure
The collection pipeline runs locally first; observed resource requirements drive the operationalization decision.
Evidence before infrastructure: the offsite's cloud-native direction stands as the likely destination, but commitment waits for measured requirements.operator, 2026-08-07
D25Doc-driven development over ticket decomposition
One functional spec per component (living markdown, 'practically pseudocode'), a top-level topology doc, and a big epic pointing at the spec — not ~100 four-hour Jira sub-tasks.
Specs drive agentic development and stay maintainable for human review; ticket trees rot as the AI restructures work. Offsite 2026-07-16.offsite decision

Program structure (live)

The program runs as coordinated pillar sessions — one dedicated working session per pillar, reporting to the coordinator, which keeps this site current. Status: collection pipeline — building; running the validated R&D tools against real inputs first, so the published-dataset shape gets decided from real record data (local-first, resource requirements measured before any operationalization choice). On-prem UI — oriented and verified through live login; holding until the insights API is specced and mocked. Data feeds — oriented, code-verified this document's delivery analysis; holding for its functional-spec brief. Platform (enterprise + enterprise_ng) — not yet launched. Autonomy — a fifth pillar building the program's coordination infrastructure (mission-control site hosting, cross-session artifact distribution).

Milestone-1 dependencies found in code (2026-08-07): the publish pipeline's config/workflows/config.yaml is CODEOWNER-gated to the release team and modification of *-publish.yaml workflows is admin-protected (creation is open) — landing the production workflow needs release-team cooperation. Working in our favor: the end-to-end feed-load validation (packages an airgap feeds.tar, boots a full Enterprise, gates on scan+policy findings) runs by default in the publish pipeline and blocks S3 upload on failure — the insights dataset inherits a real quality gate.

OSS Insights Concept/Overview

Modern software applications are made up of a large collection of open-source dependencies. A single application may pull in hundreds of OSS packages, each maintained by a different community with its own release cadence, security practices, and lifecycle. SBOMs provide the answer to an important foundational question - "what do we have installed?" - but a manifest of software alone does not provide answers to important questions that are becoming more and more relevant for practitioners looking to enhance their software supply chain security programs in the face of (even faster, with AI code generation at play) sheer numbers of OSS projects and releases skyrocketing - "are the upstream OSS projects you depend on alive, healthy, maintained, and secure?". Having technology and analysis data that can provide per-project insights across a large collection of open source projects enable organizations to move beyond inventory analysis and into a next level of risk assessment - from "what do we have installed?" to "should we be concerned about what we have?"

Building data analysis and related dev/sec/ops oriented features into an area that Anchore is calling "OSS Insights" aims to bridge that gap. The core idea is that Anchore products add features that, like existing vulnerability/malware/secrets and other security views, generate a rich dataset of OSS project analyses from publicly available sources (github, gitlab, deps.dev, many others), generate and/or ingest customer provided SBOMs, and implement techniques that map observed packages back to its canonical upstream project. With this core capability, OSS insights features can then evaluate the aspects of the OSS project itself, including (but not limited to) capturing aspects like the following:
- Is it alive, or archived/abandoned (e.g. EOL)?
- Is it actively maintained?
- How quickly has the project, historically, responded to disclosed vulnerabilities?
- Is it widely used?
- How current are its releases, and how steady is its release cadence?
- Is it extremely new, or does it even exist?

In aggregate, these qualities of any given OSS project fundamentally describes a project-health evaluation, which complements Anchore's current set of "specific package" level security and compliance assessment features.

Project-level analysis surfaces risks that most "specific package" oriented scanners do not typically include. A specific installed version of a software package may have no known CVEs or any known compliance violations today, but if the upstream project is abandoned, responds slowly to security disclosures, or has reached end-of-life, the risk is real and growing. By evaluating projects in addition to individual artifacts, features in the area of 'OSS Insights' provide a forward-looking view of supply chain health that is intended to complement existing security and compliance scanning across an organization's software surface area.

S1 — Acquisition & cataloging from third-party sources

EXISTS (alpha, rnd-projects/oss_insights_poc/alpha_stack): oss-identifiers (any identifier → canonical record; 19 ecosystems; probes deps.dev, ecosyste.ms packages+repos, ClearlyDefined, purldb, GitHub/GitLab/ Bitbucket, native registries; confidence + provenance) and oss-insight (release timeline + metrics: dne/eol booleans, first_seen/latest_release/latest_activity/vuln_fix times, active/maintained/popular). Validated: 99% enrichment, 96% repo precision, 100% fake rejection (experiment1). BUILD: productize out of rnd-projects (repo home, packaging, secrets/token management, rate-limit budget, retry/politeness policies, monitoring). Distro packages (rpm/deb/apk) explicitly out of scope → M1 pipeline. OPEN: - O1. Package universe: which purls get insights? EXISTS (precedent): software-index spec-file model (curated TOML overrides only for what cannot be derived), published-sqlite convention (ENTERPRISE-7053/7054), oss-insight {record, meta, health} envelope. EXISTS: enterprise-data-service workflow convention (build→validate→publish; KEV workflow is the closest template: fetch → jsonschema validate → archive → S3 + update listing.json); integration nightly + production 6h crons; three environments. Feed-update workflow today vs. a generic metadata-layer engine (2026-07-13)

Sources: enterprise_ng feed_update_workflow.py, scanner/db_bootstrap.py, scanner_worker.ensure_ready, jobs/policy_evaluation.py, v5 data_syncer, graph note 8a054964-c24.

Theory of operation today (vulnerability_db)

DETECTION — push. data_syncer's VulnerabilityDBDriver, after loading a new dataset record, calls ComponentCatalog client notify_feed_update() → NG POST /notify/feed-update (internal JWT route, not in APIEXT) → create_workflow(FEED_UPDATE) immediately (component_catalog.py:1388 → notify.py:133 → vulnerability_db_driver.py:75). SAFETY NET — scanner_worker.ensure_ready() (per scan batch + startup) re-checks data_syncer latest checksum vs PG vulnerability_db_state: gates scans on a current DB, converges other containers after the workflow ran elsewhere, and re-fires the workflow (checksum-debounced) if a notification was missed. Duplicates harmless (exclusive phase lock; late workflows see PG current, no-op).

WIRE FORMAT — sqlite archive per dataset version, stored by data_syncer in the object store; NG streams it directly from the object store (bypasses data_syncer's 1GB SimpleDatasetCache), imports into scanner_db_cache// with checksum marker files; atomic dir rename under exclusive META_VUL after metadata commit. vulnerability_match_exclusions_db already rides the same bootstrap as a second dataset — but as scan input (import-exclusions), not an independent layer; added ad hoc.

DIFF — grype db diff old-vs-new sqlite, STREAMED (streaming_db_diff; no full materialization) into a PAUSED rescan work queue, activated after new metadata loads. The diff exists because the grype TOOL ships a differ. Diff output = changed package identities (ecosystem/name, cpe).

RECOMPUTE — vulnerability-scan-batch consumes the queue; scan units resolved from diff identities via 4 query paths (exact name, grype_match_packages, CPE vendor:product, ownership chain). Change-set derived from the write path (was_new inserts / DELETE RETURNING), rows stamped with queue.created_at. DIFF_VALIDATE mode cross-checks diff vs background full rescan (VulnDiffValidationFailed events).

FANOUT — 4-step workflow: diff → rescan → events → enqueue-policy-evals. - events: merged change-sets → get_app_versions_for_scan_units((pm_id,distro_id)→(account,app,version), scan_started_at fence vs concurrent ingests) → one ApplicationVulnsUpdated per (account,app), 50-version cap. Delivery needs BOTH a v5 event stub AND a notifications formatter entry. - enqueue-policy-evals: queue_policy_reevaluation(targets) inserts an invalidation-placeholder PENDING row per affected app-version (API shows "stale" immediately) + one ENSURE_APP_VERSION_POLICY_EVALUATION job per app-version, each resolving its policy independently.

What is already layer-agnostic (reusable as-is)

  1. data_syncer: dataset registration/versioning/checksums/object-store storage/internal datasets API — fully dataset-agnostic; new dataset = new driver class.
  2. Job framework: register_workflow(steps), work queues + drain handlers, PAUSED→activate, per-item jobs.
  3. App-hierarchy translation: get_app_versions_for_scan_units maps package-identity changes → (account, app, version); reusable for any dataset whose changes key on package identity.
  4. Policy re-eval machinery: queue_policy_reevaluation takes generic targets; placeholder-stale rows; per-app-version jobs. Nothing vuln-specific.
  5. Event pattern: per-app event class + v5 stub + formatter (a template, not shared code).
  6. Detection pattern: checksum-vs-PG-state debounce (pattern, currently embedded in scanner ensure_ready).

What is vulnerability-specific (needs a per-layer or generalized replacement)

  1. THE DIFFER: grype db diff is an external tool. An insights dataset needs its own differ. Both are sqlite; a generic primary-key table differ (old.sqlite, new.sqlite, key columns) covers any metrics-style dataset. Contract to standardize: differ(old, new) → stream of changed identity keys.
  2. THE RECOMPUTE: vulns must RESCAN (grype matching, scanner pool, expensive). Insights need NO matching — new metadata replaces old; "what changed" IS the diff. The insights layer's step 2 collapses to a loader + the diff keys feed straight to translation. (Same 4-step workflow shape, trivial middle.)
  3. THE JOIN: (pm_id, distro_id) vs normalized base_purl — insights translation joins on purl, so a purl-keyed variant of the translator is needed (O10 normalization contract).
  4. POLICY TARGET: re-eval only matters if a gate consumes the layer. NG has only VulnerabilitiesGate; a PackagesGate consuming insights must exist before step 4 does anything for this layer.
  5. Notify wiring: the push is per-dataset (driver calls notify_feed_update; endpoint creates the vuln workflow specifically). Generalize to /notify/dataset-update {dataset_name} → METADATA_UPDATE(layer), with each data_syncer driver calling it on load — the pattern already exists, it just needs a name param. ensure_ready-style convergence for a non-scanner layer is simpler: the loader checks PG state at read time / on workflow start.

Proposed common core: "metadata layer" interface

layer = { dataset_name, schema_version, loader(archive) -> PG tables (atomic version swap), differ(old_archive, new_archive) -> stream[identity_key], # generic sqlite PK differ default translator(stream[identity_key], fence_ts) -> {(account, app_id): [version_ids]}, event_factory(app, versions, change_summary) -> AppEvent, # + v5 stub/formatter checklist policy_relevant: bool # gates step 4 } FEED_UPDATE generalizes to METADATA_UPDATE(layer): detect → load+diff → [recompute if layer needs it] → translate → events → stale-policy queue. Vulnerability layer keeps grype db diff + rescan as its custom differ/recompute; package-EOL layer uses the generic differ and no recompute. Third layer = implement the interface, zero new plumbing.

Honest sizing

~70% of the plumbing exists and is layer-agnostic (data_syncer, workflows/queues/drains, translation, policy-reeval queue, event template). The build is: (a) formalize the layer interface and de-hardcode feed_update_workflow, (b) generic sqlite differ, (c) generic notify route + driver call, (d) purl-keyed translator, (e) PackagesGate. The expensive parts of the vuln pipeline (grype matching, diff validation modes, scanner pool) are exactly the parts insights DOESN'T need.

Correction log

  • 2026-07-13: initial version claimed detection was lazy/poll-based; operator challenged; verified the push chain (driver → notify_feed_update → /notify/feed-update → create_workflow). ensure_ready is the pre-scan gate + convergence/safety net, not the trigger.
  • License swap: NO proactive handling wanted. Entitlement changes materialize at the next sync cycle (data_syncer downloads the newly-entitled dataset when it next runs; driver notifies; layer loads). Zero extra code.

OSS Insights — Data-Acquisition Deep Dive

Scope. Two halves: (1) a rigorous inventory of the third-party data sources used by the OSS Insights POC/alpha tools (/tmp/rnd-projects/oss_insights_poc/), covering interface, consumed schema, cardinality, bulk access, deltas, and licensing; (2) how vunnel solves the analogous data-acquisition problem for vulnerability data, and what of it is reusable.

Method. Code facts cite files in the cloned repos (/tmp/rnd-projects/oss_insights_poc/, /tmp/vunnel/ — fresh --depth 1 clone of https://github.com/anchore/vunnel, /tmp/enterprise-data-service/). Web facts cite the URL they came from (fetched 2026-07). Anything that is judgment rather than fact is labeled Assessment.

Half 1 — Third-party data sources used by the POC/alpha tools

1.0 How the tools consume sources (context for the per-source sections)

Three tools, one pipeline direction:

  • make_oss_identifiers (alpha_stack/make_oss_identifiers/) resolves a flexible input (PURL / forge URL / registry URL / distro filename / owner/repo) into a canonical identifier record {name, language_type, purl, source_code_url, registry_url, other_urls} by running a saturation loop of "probes" against external services and cross-checking agreement (SPEC.md §5). It is deliberately stateless: no result store; the only persistence is a requests-cache SQLite HTTP cache with a 1-hour TTL (src/oss_identifiers/default_config.toml [http] cache_ttl_seconds = 3600; SPEC.md §9).
  • make_oss_insight (alpha_stack/make_oss_insight/) takes the resolved identifier and emits release timelines + health metrics (eol, dne, active, maintained, popular, open_issues_count, first/latest release dates). Its single I/O surface is src/oss_insight/gather.py; release-timeline reconciliation on a deps.dev miss is src/oss_insight/release_sources.py. Shares the identifiers tool's HTTP cache, weekly TTL (SPEC.md §6: cache_ttl_seconds = 604800). Also stateless — "the calling pipeline owns result caching."
  • purl_summarize_depsdev (POC_stack/purl_summarize_depsdev/) is the earlier POC deps.dev client (purl_summarize_depsdev/depsdev_client.py), covering package/version/project/advisory/ dependency endpoints.

The full default source list is make_oss_identifiers/SPEC.md §13 and src/oss_identifiers/default_config.toml [aggregators]: deps.dev v3alpha, packages.ecosyste.ms, repos.ecosyste.ms, ClearlyDefined, public.purldb.io, GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket APIs, plus 19 native per-ecosystem registry APIs (§4 of the SPEC).

Observed coverage (from the alpha's own experiments) — useful cardinality ground truth:

  • make_oss_insight/COVERAGE_EXPERIMENT_RESULT.md: across 12,055 PURLs (7,000 popularity-curated via ecosyste.ms + 5,055 from real DockerHub official-image SBOMs), 91% got some enrichment; 99% for curated, 80% for SBOM-derived (misses dominated by non-published runtime-internal artifacts like JDK-internal jars).
  • make_oss_insight/COVERAGE_EXPERIMENT1_RESULT.md: on a validated 713-PURL corpus, source_code_url precision 96%, timeline completeness 96%, fake-package rejection 100%.

1.1 deps.dev (Google Open Source Insights)

Interface

  • Base: https://api.deps.dev with /v3 (stable) and /v3alpha (experimental) prefixes; JSON over HTTPS plus gRPC (https://docs.deps.dev/api/). The POC/alpha tools use v3alpha only (default_config.toml: depsdev_base = "https://api.deps.dev/v3alpha").
  • Endpoints used by the tools:
  • GET /v3alpha/purl/{url-encoded purl} — PurlLookup; unversioned PURL → package (all versions); versioned PURL → version detail. Used in probes/aggregator/depsdev.py (DepsDevPurlProbe) and oss_insight/gather.py.
  • GET /v3alpha/projects/{host/owner/repo}:packageversions — reverse lookup forge repo → packages built from it, with relationProvenance trust flags (probes/aggregator/depsdev.py DepsDevProjectProbe).
  • POC client additionally: GET /systems/{system}/packages/{name} (fallback when /purl/ 404s for some Go modules), .../versions/{version}, .../versions/{version}:dependencies (resolved graph), ...:requirements (declared deps), /projects/{key}, /advisories/{id} (purl_summarize_depsdev/depsdev_client.py).
  • Full v3alpha surface (https://docs.deps.dev/api/v3alpha/): additionally PurlLookupBatch (POST /v3alpha/purllookupbatch, max 5,000 per request), GetVersionBatch, GetProjectBatch, GetFindingsBatch, GetDependents, GetCapabilities (Go only), GetSimilarlyNamedPackages (typosquats), QueryContainerImages. Note: purl lookup is v3alpha-only — not in stable v3 (https://docs.deps.dev/api/v3/).
  • Auth: none. "Free and immediately available — no need to register for an API key" (https://blog.deps.dev/api/). API usage governed by Google API ToS (https://docs.deps.dev/api/v3/). Clients "expressly permitted to cache data served by the API" (same page).
  • Rate limits: none documented anywhere in docs.deps.dev or the GitHub README. The tools' code contains no deps.dev-specific throttle handling beyond the generic error classes.

Schema consumed by the tools

API field Consumer Use
package.name DepsDevPurlProbe canonical name evidence (conf 0.8)
versions[].isDefault, versions[].versionKey.version gather.py, depsdev.py pick default version; releases.latest
versions[].publishedAt version_history.py (POC) release timeline dates
version.links[] (label=SOURCE_REPO/HOMEPAGE/ORIGIN, url) DepsDevPurlProbe source_code_url (conf 0.85), homepage
version.relatedProjects[].project.projectKey.id DepsDevPurlProbe derive forge URL forms
version.isDeprecated oss_insight metrics (SPEC.md §4) eol metric
version.advisoryKeys oss_insight metrics vuln_fix placeholder metric
versions[].versionKey.{system,name} + relationProvenance DepsDevProjectProbe repo→package candidates; trusted provenance set incl. PYPI_PUBLISH_ATTESTATION, NPM_PROVENANCE, GO_ORIGIN, SLSA_ATTESTATION, …
project scorecard, stars depsdev_client.get_project (POC) fetched; summarization only

Cardinality

  • Ecosystems: Go, RubyGems, npm, Cargo, Maven, PyPI, NuGet (system enum, https://docs.deps.dev/api/v3/; FAQ https://docs.deps.dev/faq/). Hex appears in the alpha's DEPSDEV_SYSTEMS set (probes/aggregator/depsdev.py) — the /purl/ endpoint accepts pkg:hex/... in practice, though hex is not in the documented v3 system enum.
  • Scale (dated blog figures; no current official total): >50M package versions / ~5M packages at API launch (2023-04, https://blog.deps.dev/api/); +350k NuGet packages (https://blog.deps.dev/nuget/); +184k RubyGems / 1.8M versions (https://blog.deps.dev/rubygems/). Maven coverage includes Maven Central plus Google, Jenkins and Gradle Plugins repos (https://github.com/google/deps.dev).
  • Observed in the alpha experiments: deps.dev hit-rate is high for popular packages in its 7 ecosystems but misses the Go long tail (hence the Go-module-proxy fallback in release_sources.py) and covers none of the other 12 alpha ecosystems (hex partial).

Bulk access

  • BigQuery public dataset bigquery-public-data.deps_dev_v1 (docs: https://docs.deps.dev/bigquery/v1/; Marketplace: https://console.cloud.google.com/marketplace/product/bigquery-public-data/deps-dev). Tables: PackageVersions, Projects, PackageVersionToProject, Dependencies, DependencyGraphEdges, Dependents, Advisories, PackageVersionHashes, NuGetRequirements, RubyGemsRequirements — each with a ...Latest view, plus a Snapshots table listing timestamps at which full snapshots of all tables exist.
  • Historical snapshots are retained keyed by SnapshotAt; snapshot cadence is not documented — must be read empirically from the Snapshots table. Do not assume "daily" without checking.
  • No downloadable dumps / GCS bucket exist — BigQuery is the only official bulk channel (checked https://docs.deps.dev/ and the GitHub README).

Diffs / deltas

  • No incremental change feed. The live API keeps actively-updated packages fresh "within an hour or so" plus a constant-rate background rescan; "There is no mechanism for users to trigger an update" (https://docs.deps.dev/faq/).
  • Realistic incremental strategy (assessment): diff successive BigQuery snapshots (SnapshotAt keyed) server-side in SQL — cheap and exact; or re-poll the live API per-package on our own schedule (batch endpoints, 5,000/request, help a lot).

Licensing

  • "This generated data is available under a CC-BY 4.0 license." — verbatim in both https://github.com/google/deps.dev (README) and https://docs.deps.dev/bigquery/v1/.
  • Scoping nuance: CC-BY covers deps.dev's generated data (resolved graphs, project↔package mappings, etc.). Data sourced from registries "with their respective terms" is not relicensed — upstream registry terms still apply to those fields (same sources).
  • Commercial redistribution: CC-BY 4.0 permits commercial use/redistribution with attribution. API usage itself is under Google API ToS (https://developers.google.com/terms). License risk: LOW (attribution required; assess upstream-registry terms for pass-through fields like descriptions).

1.2 ecosyste.ms (packages + repos)

Interface

  • packages: https://packages.ecosyste.ms/api/v1; repos: https://repos.ecosyste.ms/api/v1 (default_config.toml [aggregators]). OpenAPI specs at https://{packages,repos}.ecosyste.ms/docs/api/v1/openapi.yaml (mirrored in https://github.com/ecosyste-ms/packages and .../repos). Note: the /docs pages sit behind Anubis anti-bot proof-of-work protection; plain curl passes but headless fetchers may not — relevant to any scraper design.
  • Endpoints used by the tools:
  • GET /api/v1/registries/{ecosystems_id}/packages/{name} (probes/aggregator/ecosystems.py EcosystemsPackageProbe; maven names encoded group:artifact, npm scoped @scope/name).
  • GET /api/v1/repositories/lookup?url={repo_url} on repos.ecosyste.ms (EcosystemsRepoLookupProbe) — reverse repo→packages.
  • {versions_url}?per_page=100&page=N — paged version list, used as the supporting release source and last-resort timeline (oss_insight/release_sources.py _ecosystems, capped at 20 pages).
  • Wider API surface (OpenAPI): GET /registries, GET /registries/{r}/packages with created_after/updated_after/sort params, purl lookup GET /packages/lookup?purl=…, bulk POST /packages/bulk_lookup (purls array, max 100), /packages/critical, maintainers/namespaces; repos side: /hosts, /hosts/{h}/repositories (with updated_after, sort, order), per-repo /tags, /releases, /manifests, /sbom.
  • Sibling services (one-liners, from https://ecosyste.ms/): commits.ecosyste.ms (889M commits / 6.33M repos), issues.ecosyste.ms (32.9M issues / 109M PRs), advisories, docker, timeline, summary — all https://{service}.ecosyste.ms/api/v1 per https://ecosyste.ms/api.
  • Auth & rate limits: no key required. Repo READMEs say "default rate limit … 5000/req per hour based on your IP" (https://github.com/ecosyste-ms/packages). The newer pricing page (https://ecosyste.ms/pricing) lists Free = 300 req/hr (polite/common pools), Develop $200/mo = 1,000 req/hr + API key, Scale $1,000/mo = 5,000 req/hr + commercial SLA. Polite pool: include mailto= param, mailto in User-Agent, or From header (https://ecosyste.ms/api). The two statements conflict; the pricing page appears to be current policy.

Schema consumed by the tools

API field Consumer Use
name EcosystemsPackageProbe name evidence (maven: strip group: prefix)
repository_url same source_code_url evidence (conf 0.8)
homepage, documentation_url same other URLs
language both probes language_type evidence
packages[0].{registry.name, name} (repos lookup) EcosystemsRepoLookupProbe repo→package candidate (first entry only, to avoid fork noise)
versions_url; versions number, published_at release_sources._ecosystems supporting/last-resort release timeline
purl, download-ranked package lists experiment corpus builders corpus construction

Cardinality

Front pages, fetched 2026-07: packages.ecosyste.ms = 109 registries, 51 ecosystems, 14.45M packages, 164.3M versions; repos.ecosyste.ms = 1,954 hosts, 292.7M repositories. This is the broadest package aggregator available — it is the alpha's coverage backstop for the 12 ecosystems deps.dev lacks (hackage, hex, pub, cran, bioconductor, conda, swift, nix, opam, luarocks, composer, swipl — see SPEC.md §4 and probes/aggregator/ecosystems.py docstring).

Bulk access

  • https://packages.ecosyste.ms/open-data — full-database dumps. Latest release 2026-02-05: https://ecosystems-data.s3.amazonaws.com/packages-2026-02-05.tar.gz, ~13.1M packages, ~63.7 GB (verified via HTTP HEAD). Format verified by extraction: a PostgreSQL pg_dump export (packages-2026-02-05.sql + license.txt CC BY-SA 4.0 text), not parquet/NDJSON. Cadence irregular (prior: 2024-06-04, 2024-03-01) — not a scheduled feed.
  • https://repos.ecosyste.ms/open-data is stale: latest 2023-08-30 (~168.5M repos vs today's 292.7M). issues open-data similarly stale (2023-08-23).
  • One-off Zenodo NDJSON extract exists (https://zenodo.org/records/10045415) — not recurring.

Diffs / deltas

  • Yes, natively: list endpoints accept updated_after + sort=updated_at&order=asc on both packages and repos APIs (verified in both OpenAPI specs) — a clean incremental cursor: GET /registries/{r}/packages?updated_after=<ts>&sort=updated_at&order=asc.
  • Upstream freshness model documented in https://github.com/ecosyste-ms/packages/blob/main/docs/syncing.md (registry RSS polling every 5–15 min, cross-service pings, stale-package sweeps) — explicitly best-effort, no commitments.

Licensing — the flagged one

  • Data: CC BY-SA 4.0 (code AGPL-3). Stated in site footers, both READMEs, OpenAPI spec license fields, the open-data listings, and the license text inside the dump tarball (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
  • https://ecosyste.ms/commercial: data is licensed "to ensure that the community can use the services … if you contribute your work back to that same community. To operate an instance of ecosyste.ms or utilise ecosyste.ms' data for your own use, we offer paid plans and less restrictive licences." The published paid tiers still list CC BY-SA as the data license; the less-restrictive license is a contact-us arrangement, not a listed SKU.
  • ecosyste.ms is a nonprofit hosted by Open Source Collective (https://ecosyste.ms/about).
  • License risk: HIGH for a proprietary paid dataset. ShareAlike means adapted material built from this data must be redistributed under CC BY-SA (or compatible). Repackaging into a closed, paid Anchore dataset is not compatible with the default license; options are (a) negotiate the commercial license they explicitly offer, (b) restrict use to facts-not-database-extraction arguments (assessment: legally murky, don't rely on it), or (c) treat ecosyste.ms as a discovery/QA aid rather than a redistributed source. Note the older repos/issues dumps are labeled plain "CC-BY" on their open-data pages — a labeling inconsistency worth citing precisely in any legal review.

1.3 ClearlyDefined

Interface (docs, verified live 2026-07-13)

  • Base: https://api.clearlydefined.io/ (dev: https://dev-api.clearlydefined.io/); Swagger UI at https://api.clearlydefined.io/api-docs/; usage docs at https://docs.clearlydefined.io/docs/get-involved/using-data. OpenAPI spec: https://github.com/clearlydefined/service/blob/master/schemas/swagger.yaml.
  • GET /definitions/{type}/{provider}/{namespace}/{name}/{revision} (coordinates model: - for empty namespace; git components keyed by commit hash). Also GET /definitions?pattern= (search), POST /definitions (batch), /curations/..., POST /harvest, /notices.
  • Auth: none for reads (verified live). Rate limits (documented): 2,000 req/min for reads; 250/min for POST /definitions, /curations, /notices; HTTP 429 with x-ratelimit-* headers (https://docs.clearlydefined.io/docs/get-involved/using-data).
  • Data: described (releaseDate, sourceLocation, urls, hashes, tools, scores) and licensed (declared SPDX expression, discovered expressions, attribution parties, per-facet scores) + per-file hashes/license findings (verified live on npm/npmjs/-/lodash/4.17.21).

Cardinality

GET https://api.clearlydefined.io/stats/total (live 2026-07-13, endpoint not in the published swagger — treat as unofficial): 55,196,539 definitions, across types conda, condasrc, crate, gem, git, maven, npm, nuget, pod, composer, pypi, deb, debsrc. Median licensed score 60.

Bulk access & diffs

  • Yes, and it has a real delta feed: hourly changeset snapshot store on Azure blob — GET {base}/changes/index (changeset list, named yyyy-mm-dd-hh since 2019), GET {base}/changes/{changeset} (changed coordinates), GET {base}/{coordinates}.json (changed definition, files excluded). Production base: https://clearlydefinedprod.blob.core.windows.net/changes-notifications. Doc: https://github.com/clearlydefined/service/blob/master/docs/change-notification-api.md. Definitions only (no harvested raw data or curations).

Licensing

  • CC0 for all data ("all the data is distributed under CC0", https://docs.clearlydefined.io/docs/resources/faq; curated-data repo LICENSE is CC0). Code is MIT. License risk: NONE — public-domain dedication, no attribution required, commercial redistribution unrestricted.

Interface (code)

  • GET https://api.clearlydefined.io/definitions/{type}/{provider}/{namespace}/{name}/{revision} with - as namespace placeholder and - as revision to get the aggregate definition (probes/aggregator/clearlydefined.py). No auth in code.
  • Type/provider mapping in code (CD_MAP): pypi/pypi, npm/npmjs, gem/rubygems, crate/cratesio, maven/mavencentral, nuget/nuget, composer/packagist, go/golang.
  • Behavioral trap documented in the probe docstring: ClearlyDefined returns HTTP 200 with a synthetic echo response even for coordinates it has never scanned; real data is distinguished by non-empty described.tools (the scanner-tools list).

Schema consumed

API field Use
described.tools real-vs-synthetic discriminator
described.sourceLocation.{provider,namespace,name} source_code_url (GitHub only, conf 0.85)
described.projectWebsite, described.issueTracker homepage / issue-tracker URLs
coordinates.name name canonicalization

1.4 purldb (public.purldb.io — AboutCode/nexB)

Interface (docs, verified live 2026-07-13)

  • Public instance https://public.purldb.io/api/ (Swagger: /api/docs/; docs: https://purldb.readthedocs.io/en/latest/purldb/rest_api.html). Endpoints from the live API root: packages/, update_packages/, package_sets/, resources/, validate/, collect/ (fetch-on-miss: mines a missing package on demand), watch/, scan_queue/, to_purl/, from_purl/, matching/.
  • Auth: none currently on the public instance (verified live: anonymous packages/ and collect/ return 200). Token auth exists but is disabled by default (PURLDB_SETTINGS_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATION); only scan_queue needs a special key. No documented rate limits.

Cardinality

Live 2026-07-13: GET /api/packages/?page_size=1 → count: 21,912,790 packages. Rich fields per package (verified on lodash@4.17.21): purl decomposition, primary_language, description, parties, homepage/download/vcs URLs, sha1/256/512/md5, copyright/holder, declared_license_expression(_spdx), scancode license_detections, package_sets. (In the alpha's experience many metadata fields are often null — probes/aggregator/purldb.py docstring.)

Bulk access & diffs

  • No public bulk dump of public.purldb.io; API pagination or self-hosting the open-source stack (PackageDB/MineCode/MatchCode, https://github.com/aboutcode-org/purldb) are the bulk options. No change feed; watch/ exists for registry watching in self-hosted deployments.

Licensing

  • NOTICE file (https://github.com/aboutcode-org/purldb/blob/main/NOTICE): "purldb software is licensed under the Apache License version 2.0. purldb data is licensed collectively under CC-BY-SA-4.0." License risk: HIGH for proprietary repackaging — same share-alike constraint as ecosyste.ms.

Interface (code)

  • GET https://public.purldb.io/api/packages/?purl={encoded} (probes/aggregator/purldb.py). No auth in code; probe is toggleable via purldb_enabled in config.
  • Code-documented quirks: the filter is loose (returns adjacent/similarly-named packages — the probe re-filters strictly on exact PURL prefix), and repository_url / primary_language "are often null in PurlDB responses" (module docstring). Its primary value in the alpha is existence corroboration (purl_exists, conf 0.9), not metadata.

Schema consumed

results[].{purl, name, homepage_url, download_url, repository_url, primary_language} (probes/aggregator/purldb.py).

1.5 endoflife.date

Interface (docs, verified live 2026-07-13)

  • v1 API: https://endoflife.date/api/v1 (OpenAPI 3.1.1, spec https://endoflife.date/docs/api/v1/openapi.yml, Swagger UI https://endoflife.date/docs/api/v1/). Paths: /products, /products/full, /products/{product}, /products/{product}/releases/{release}, .../releases/latest, /categories, /tags, /identifiers, /identifiers/{identifier_type}.
  • Legacy API still live: GET https://endoflife.date/api/{product}.json (bare cycle array) and /api/all.json. No auth, no documented rate limits on either version.
  • Response shape (verified live, /api/v1/products/python/releases/3.12): {name, releaseDate, isLts, isEol, eolFrom, isMaintained, latest{name,...}, custom{...}}; products carry identifiers as purl lists (e.g. pkg:generic/python, pkg:deb/ubuntu/python3.12) — directly joinable to package identity.

Cardinality

460 products (homepage statement + total: 460 from /api/v1/products + 460 files in products/, all verified 2026-07-13). Product/OS/runtime-level, not per-library.

Bulk access & diffs

  • The site is a git repo: https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date — Jekyll site with products/*.md, each product a YAML-frontmatter markdown file (title, category, versionCommand, releasePolicyLink, identifiers/purls, release-cycle entries — verified on products/python.md). Version freshness is automated by https://github.com/endoflife-date/release-data (MIT) via bots.
  • Diffs: git history is the delta mechanism; no API change feed. API responses carry generated_at and per-product last_modified for staleness checks. A full-corpus fetch is one call (/api/v1/products/full) — delta machinery is barely needed at this size.

Licensing

  • MIT for the whole repo including product data (https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/blob/master/LICENSE; GitHub reports SPDX MIT for both repos). No CC-BY-SA claim found on site or repo. License risk: NONE (attribution/license-notice preservation only; explicit right to "distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies").

Note: the POC/alpha tools do not query endoflife.date — the alpha's eol metric is derived from deps.dev isDeprecated + GitHub archived (make_oss_insight/SPEC.md §4). endoflife.date enters the picture via vunnel, which already ships an eol provider consuming https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/full (see §2.1 below) — product/OS-level EOL, not per-package.

1.6 Forge APIs (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket)

Interface

  • GitHub REST: GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo} (probes/forge/github.py; oss_insight/gather.py), and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases?per_page=100&page=N (paged, cap 20 pages) as an authoritative release source (release_sources._github_releases). Auth: optional GITHUB_TOKEN auto-attached by the shared HttpClient (src/oss_identifiers/http.py lines 102–106). Documented rate limits: 60 req/hr unauthenticated per IP, 5,000 req/hr with a token (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api).
  • GitLab: GET https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/{owner}%2F{repo} (probes/forge/gitlab.py), no auth in code.
  • Bitbucket: GET https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{owner}/{repo} (probes/forge/bitbucket.py), no auth in code.

Schema consumed

GitHub: html_url (canonical-case repo URL), name, language, homepage, archived (conf 1.0 → feeds eol), plus in oss-insight pushed_at (→ latest_activity), stargazers_count (→ popular), open_issues_count (issues+PRs conflated — caveat documented in SPEC.md §4). Releases: tag_name, published_at, draft. GitLab: web_url, homepage-ish fields. Bitbucket: links.html.href, website, language.

Bulk / deltas / licensing

  • No bulk story relevant here; per-repo API only. GH Archive/GHTorrent exist for events but are out of scope for what the tools consume.
  • Assessment: forge metadata (stars, archived, pushed_at) is the piece with no aggregator substitute at full fidelity; ecosyste.ms repos mirrors much of it (CC BY-SA problem), deps.dev /projects mirrors scorecard/stars for its ecosystems (CC-BY). GitHub's ToS restrict wholesale scraping/resale of GitHub data; per-repo metadata used to compute derived health metrics is the defensible pattern (label: assessment, not legal advice).

1.7 Native per-ecosystem registry APIs (+ Go module proxy)

The alpha treats the package's own registry as the authoritative source for existence, canonical name, and (in oss-insight) release timelines. Endpoints, from src/oss_identifiers/default_config.toml (registry_api per purl_types.*) and probes/registry_native/*.py, oss_insight/release_sources.py:

Ecosystem Endpoint(s) used Notes
PyPI https://pypi.org/pypi/{name}/json PEP 503 normalization
npm https://registry.npmjs.org/{name} scoped names
RubyGems https://rubygems.org/api/v1/gems/{name}.json
crates.io https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/{name}
Maven https://search.maven.org/solrsearch/select?q=g:"{ns}"+AND+a:"{name}" Central search
NuGet https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/{name}/index.json
Packagist https://repo.packagist.org/p2/{ns}/{name}.json release timeline source; dev- filtered
Go https://proxy.golang.org/{module}/@latest, @v/list + @v/{v}.info !-case encoding; timeline capped at 100 versions (release_sources._go_proxy); fills deps.dev's Go long tail
Hackage https://hackage.haskell.org/package/{name}
Hex https://hex.pm/api/packages/{name} timeline: releases[].{version,inserted_at}
pub.dev https://pub.dev/api/packages/{name} timeline: versions[].{version,published}
LuaRocks https://luarocks.org/modules/{ns}/{name} HTML
opam https://opam.ocaml.org/packages/{name} opam DSL
CRAN https://crandb.r-pkg.org/{name}/all METACRAN; timeline map version→date
Bioconductor https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/{name}.html HTML scrape
