  • Auth: none for any of these in code (SPEC §13 table: Auth = none throughout).
  • Cardinality: each registry is by definition 100% authoritative for its own ecosystem; sizes per ecosyste.ms front page (164M versions across 109 registries) give the union upper bound.
  • Bulk: varies wildly per registry (out of the tools' scope). Notable: PyPI offers a BigQuery public dataset; npm offers the replicate.npmjs.com CouchDB _changes feed; crates.io publishes daily DB dumps (https://static.crates.io/db-dump.tar.gz); Maven Central has an index. Assessment: you would not build bulk ingestion on 19 bespoke registry pipelines in v1 — that is exactly the aggregation work deps.dev/ecosyste.ms already do; native registries are the verification/gap-fill tier, which is precisely the role the alpha assigns them.
  • Deltas: npm _changes is a true event feed; most others are poll-only. The alpha polls with an HTTP cache.
  • Licensing: registry metadata terms differ per registry (e.g. npm public registry terms, PyPI ToS); the alpha consumes only facts (name/URLs/versions/dates). Assessment: facts about releases (version strings + dates) carry minimal copyright risk; descriptions and readmes would carry more — the tools deliberately do not harvest those.

Half 2 — How vunnel solves the same problem for vulnerability data

vunnel (https://github.com/anchore/vunnel, Apache-2.0, clone at /tmp/vunnel) is "a tool for fetching, transforming, and storing vulnerability data from a variety of sources" (README.md). 27 providers ship in-tree (src/vunnel/providers/): alma, alpine, amazon, arch, bitnami, chainguard(+libraries), debian, echo, eol, epss, fedora, github, govulndb, hummingbird, kev, mariner, minimos, nvd, oracle, photon, rhel, rocky, secureos, sles, ubuntu, wolfi.

2.1 Provider framework

A provider subclasses vunnel.provider.Provider (src/vunnel/provider.py) and implements exactly two things (DEVELOPING.md "Adding a new provider"):

  • name() — unique provider id (= workspace dir name)
  • update(last_updated: datetime | None) -> tuple[list[str], int] — "populates the input directory from external sources, processes the data, places results into the output directory" (provider.py:177-180), returning (urls consulted, result count).

Everything else is framework:

  • Workspace (src/vunnel/workspace.py): each provider owns <root>/<name>/{input/, results/, metadata.json, checksums}. input/ holds raw downloads; results/ holds normalized records; metadata.json is the State dataclass — {provider, urls, store, timestamp, version, distribution_version, processor ("vunnel@<version>"), listing (xxh64 digest of a file-listing), schema, stale}. checksums is a tab-delimited xxh64 path listing of every result file, itself digested into State.listing — the whole workspace is content-addressed and tamper-evident (Workspace.validate_checksums, write_file_listing).
  • Runtime policy (provider.py RuntimeConfig): declarative knobs for existing_input/existing_results (keep/delete), on_error (fail/skip/retry + retry_count/delay + what to do with input/results state on error), and result_store (flat-file vs sqlite).
  • Versioning: class-level __version__ (processing semantics) and __distribution_version__ (result-schema breaking changes). If the recorded state's version differs from the code's, Provider.run() clears the workspace and starts clean (provider.py:271-291) — automatic cache invalidation on schema/behavior change.
  • HTTP layer (src/vunnel/utils/http_wrapper.py): shared get() with retries, exponential backoff, per-host connection pooling, and per-host rate-limit state honoring Retry-After on 429/503 (HostState.blocked_until, HostRegistry). Providers do not hand-roll politeness.
  • There is no formal fetch/parse/normalize interface — the convention is a Manager/Parser class per provider doing download→parse, with update() streaming normalized records into self.results_writer() (see providers/eol/manager.py, providers/nvd/manager.py).

The eol provider is a working template for insights-shaped data (providers/eol/): fetches https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/full in one call, passes each product/cycle through with minimal transformation ("passthrough approach", DEVELOPING.md there), writes one record per product:cycle under an eol schema whose JSON Schema is generated from endoflife.date's OpenAPI spec (generate_schema.py fetches https://endoflife.date/docs/api/v1/openapi.yml and extracts ProductRelease). Fields: product, identifiers, name, codename, label, releaseDate, isLts, ltsFrom, isEoas, eoasFrom, isEol, eolFrom, isDiscontinued, discontinuedFrom, isEoes, eoesFrom, isMaintained, latest, custom (schema/eol/schema-1.0.0.json). It is tagged auxiliary — the tags mechanism (provider.py HasTags) already distinguishes non-vulnerability providers.

2.2 Incremental refresh — the actual mechanism

Three cooperating layers:

  1. Workspace state timestamp. Provider._update() reads metadata.json; if state exists and is not stale, it passes state.timestamp as last_updated into the provider's update() (provider.py:188-201). That timestamp is the only cross-run input-state the framework itself supplies. Providers opt in to using it:
  2. NVD (providers/nvd/manager.py): if the input sqlite exists and last_updated is within the API's max date-range window, it calls the NVD API with lastModStartDate/lastModEndDate (api.py:88-91) and merges updated CVEs into the kept input db (_can_update_incrementally, _download_updates); otherwise full re-download.
  3. GitHub (providers/github/parser.py): keeps its own timestamp + GraphQL cursor in a metadata db in input/ and asks the GHSA GraphQL API only for advisories updated since then; tagged "incremental" (providers/github/__init__.py).
  4. Simple providers (eol, epss, wolfi…) ignore last_updated and re-download — fine when the upstream is one bounded file.
  5. Kept input dir + result store as cache. existing_input: keep (default) means raw downloads persist between runs; providers use skip_if_exists to avoid re-fetching files already present. Results with ResultStatePolicy.KEEP accumulate; sqlite stores upsert (INSERT OR REPLACE, result.py:227) so an incremental run only rewrites changed records.
  6. Import-results mode (distribution-level increment). Instead of computing at all, a provider can be configured with import_results_* to download a previously-built results archive from a hosted listing (listing.json → ListingDocument, src/vunnel/distribution.py), compare enclosed_checksum against local state (_has_newer_archive, provider.py:241-256) and only fetch when the archive actually changed. This is how downstream consumers skip recomputation entirely; state is marked stale=true so the next layer knows the timestamp is inherited.

There is no HTTP-level etag/if-modified-since cache in the framework (unlike the alpha tools' requests-cache); freshness economy comes from provider-level "updated-since" queries and archive-checksum comparison.

2.3 Result storage, format, and schema versioning

  • Records are written through result.Writer.write(identifier, schema, payload) which wraps every payload in an Envelope{schema: <schema URL>, identifier, item} (result.py:33-37, 346-354) — every stored record self-describes its schema version via a URL like https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/vunnel/main/schema/eol/schema-1.0.0.json (src/vunnel/schema.py; JSON Schema documents live in /tmp/vunnel/schema/).
  • Two store strategies (result.py):
  • FLAT_FILE: one JSON file per record under results/ (nested dirs allowed via / in the identifier — e.g. github writes github:pypi/ghsa-....json).
  • SQLITE: a single results/results.db with table results(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, record BLOB) — the record blob is the orjson-serialized Envelope. Batched writes (5,000), WAL mode, written to results.db.tmp then atomically moved on successful close (SQLiteStore.close). Read back via SQLiteReader.each().
  • Schema constants per family: OS_SCHEMA_VERSION 1.1.0, NVD 1.0.1, OSV 1.6.1, GHSA 1.0.3, EPSS 1.0.0, EOL 1.0.0, etc. (schema.py:7-20). A breaking result-schema change bumps the provider's __distribution_version__, which flows into metadata.json and into the distribution listing so consumers can select compatible archives (distribution.ListingDocument.latest_entry(schema_version=...)).

2.4 How grype-db consumes provider output (interface level)

  • grype-db is pointed at the vunnel root: provider.root: data/vunnel plus a configs: list of provider names (/tmp/enterprise-data-service/config/grype-db/config.yaml). For each provider it reads data/vunnel/<name>/metadata.json (timestamps, urls, schema/version) and iterates results/ (flat files or results.db), interpreting each Envelope by its schema URL, and transforms records into the final grype sqlite DB.
  • grype-db can also drive vunnel: grype-db pull -p <provider> shells out to vunnel using provider.vunnel.config: config/vunnel/vunnel.yaml and executor: direct (same config.yaml, incl. env passthrough for NVD_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN).
  • grype-db cache backup/restore/status archives and restores the whole per-provider workspace (input + results + metadata + checksums) as grype-db-cache.tar.gz — the unit of cache exchange used by EDS below.
  • Contract summary (this is the reusable seam): a provider directory with metadata.json + checksummed results in a self-described schema is the entire interface between acquisition and build.

2.5 EDS orchestration and the S3 provider cache

From /tmp/enterprise-data-service/:

  • Config: config/vunnel/vunnel.yaml (root data/vunnel; NVD api key, GitHub token, ubuntu max_workers: 128), config/grype-db/config.yaml (27 providers incl. proprietary anchore-match-exclusions, msrc).
  • Per-provider daily refresh, in a GitHub Actions matrix — one job per provider (.github/workflows/grype-db-publish.yaml), each job doing (taskfile.d/grype-db.yaml):
  • download-provider-cache — read s3://<bucket>/providers/<provider>/latest (a small object holding a datestamp), then fetch s3://<bucket>/providers/<provider>/<date>/grype-db-cache.tar.gz and grype-db cache restore it into data/vunnel/. Bucket: enterprise-data-service.production.anchore.io (config/grype-db-manager/production.yaml).
  • refresh-provider-cache — grype-db pull -v -p <provider> (runs vunnel update() on top of the restored workspace — this is where incremental logic actually pays off: NVD/GitHub only pull changes since the cached state's timestamp).
  • upload-provider-cache — grype-db cache backup → upload to a new dated S3 path and rewrite latest.
  • The build job then runs download-all-provider-cache (.github/scripts/download-all-provider-cache.py) to aggregate every provider's latest archive, and grype-db build/build-and-upload produces the final DB. There is also an apply-provider-patches-to-cache step that copies hand-maintained patch files from S3 into <provider>/input/legacy/ before refresh.
  • Net effect: provider caches are durable, dated, per-provider S3 artifacts; each daily run is warm-start (restore → incremental update → re-upload), and a provider failure doesn't poison others (matrix isolation + per-provider Slack alert in the workflow).

2.6 Reusability assessment for an insights pipeline — honest take

What maps cleanly (copy these patterns, or the code itself):

  1. Workspace/state model (workspace.py) — input/results split, metadata.json with timestamp/urls/versions, xxh64 checksummed listings. Nothing vuln-specific in this file.
  2. Result store + Envelope (result.py) — schema-URL-tagged records, flat-file or sqlite, atomic tmp→final move, upsert semantics. Also content-agnostic.
  3. Incremental contract — update(last_updated) + kept input + per-provider opt-in updated-since logic. Maps directly: ecosyste.ms has updated_after (like NVD's lastModStartDate), deps.dev needs snapshot-diffing (like providers that re-download bounded files), registries are poll-only.
  4. Version-bump-clears-workspace invalidation (provider.py:271-291).
  5. The S3 dated per-provider cache + warm-start matrix orchestration (EDS taskfile + workflow) — wholesale reusable for any provider-shaped pipeline.
  6. Distribution listing (distribution.py, listing.json + checksums + import-results mode) if the insights dataset is shipped to customers the way grype DBs are.
  7. http_wrapper — retry/backoff/Retry-After/per-host pooling, exactly what polite aggregator polling needs.

What does not fit:

  1. The record schemas. All vunnel schemas except eol/epss are vuln-record-shaped (schema/vulnerability/...). Insights records (package identity, release timeline, health metrics) need new JSON Schemas — but the eol provider proves the framework carries non-vulnerability payloads without any framework change (new schema/<family>/ dir + a Schema factory in schema.py).
  2. Grain and fan-out. vunnel providers enumerate a source's records (one bounded corpus per provider: all CVEs, all GHSAs, all EOL cycles). The insights alpha is query-shaped: resolve one input PURL by fanning out to N sources with cross-checking (saturation loop, confidence scoring — make_oss_identifiers/SPEC.md §5). That per-package resolve/reconcile logic has no vunnel analogue and would live inside an insights provider's update() (iterate the package universe, resolve each) or upstream of it. Assessment: the practical decomposition is per-source providers (deps.dev snapshot, ecosyste.ms delta puller, endoflife.date passthrough, registry timelines) + a downstream reconciliation/build step where the oss-identifiers/oss-insight logic runs — mirroring vunnel(fetch/normalize) vs grype-db(merge/build).
  3. Downstream consumer. grype-db's schema-driven build obviously doesn't apply; the insights equivalent (per-package rollup into a queryable artifact) must be new.
  4. Scale profile. vunnel's biggest corpus (NVD, ~300k CVEs) is small next to "all packages" (14M packages / 164M versions at ecosyste.ms scale). The flat-file store would not survive that; the sqlite store plausibly does (it already batches and upserts), but per-provider dumps/BigQuery bulk ingestion (not per-package REST crawling) has to be the primary acquisition mode for the universe-scale sources. Assessment, supported by the rate-limit math: at ecosyste.ms's paid 5,000 req/hr, 14M packages ≈ 117 days per full pass — API crawling can only ever be the delta/verification tier.

Vunnel provider vs parallel framework? Assessment: an insights provider can literally be a vunnel provider (eol already is one, and the tags() mechanism separates auxiliary providers from vulnerability ones), and for endoflife.date-style bounded sources that is the cheapest path — EDS orchestration would pick it up with a one-line matrix addition. But the universe-scale sources (deps.dev BigQuery, ecosyste.ms pg dump) want bulk-ingest steps that don't look like update() HTTP fetching, and coupling insights release cadence/schema evolution to the grype-db data pipeline repo has organizational costs. The pragmatic call: reuse the vunnel patterns (and lift workspace.py/result.py/http_wrapper.py nearly verbatim) in an insights-specific pipeline repo, and only implement bounded auxiliary sources (endoflife.date) as actual vunnel providers if grype/EDS also wants them.

What to copy from vunnel

  1. workspace.py — input/results dirs, metadata.json State (timestamp/urls/version/stale), xxh64 checksum listings. Copy nearly verbatim.
  2. result.py — schema-URL Envelope, sqlite store with batch/upsert/atomic-replace, SQLiteReader. Copy nearly verbatim.
  3. The update(last_updated) -> (urls, count) provider contract + RuntimeConfig keep/delete/on-error policies + version-bump-clears-workspace invalidation.
  4. NVD's incremental pattern (_can_update_incrementally + updated-since API window + upsert into kept input db) — direct template for an ecosyste.ms updated_after puller.
  5. The eol provider wholesale — it already ingests endoflife.date v1 products/full with a generated schema; extend rather than reimplement.
  6. http_wrapper.py — retry/backoff/Retry-After/per-host pooling.
  7. EDS's per-provider dated S3 cache + latest pointer + warm-start matrix (taskfile.d/grype-db.yaml: download-cache → pull → upload-cache), and the distribution.py listing.json pattern if the dataset ships to customers.
  8. Schema-per-family JSON Schema dir + __distribution_version__ gating for breaking changes.

What NOT to inherit: vuln-shaped record schemas; per-record REST crawling as the primary acquisition mode for universe-scale sources (use BigQuery/pg-dump bulk + API deltas); grype-db's build layer.

OSS Insights — Data Schema & Middleware Design (S2/S4-slice, S7, S8) (2026-07-13)

Scope: the sqlite dataset shipped through the data service ("middleware"), the enterprise Postgres schema in NG component_catalog, the package↔insights junction decision, the four API endpoints the UI boards need, and the load/refresh pipeline against the metadata-layer interface from feed-update-analysis.md. Facts are cited as file:line from /workspace/enterprise_ng (and one v5 citation). Non-cited judgments are labeled [assessment].

Companion docs: 30k-view.md (stages S1–S9, opens O1–O22), feed-update-analysis.md (layer interface), design boards design-29634/29633/30868.png, POC oss-insight SPEC.md.

0. Ground truth from the code (the facts everything below builds on)

The ownership chain. Package (dedup by (name, version, type, base_purl), package.py:76-84) ← PackageMetadata (per-qualifier/CPE variant, dedup (package_id, content_hash), package.py:128-131) ← ArtifactPackage (junction to Artifact, package.py:137-164) → Artifact (content-addressed SBOM/image, artifact.py:23-73) ← Assets.artifact_uuid (application_manager.py:152, 176-179) → AppVersion (Assets.app_version_uuid, application_manager.py:149, 167-171) → App. Every read path walks this chain: the DAO base query (dao/packages.py:927-943), the packages CTE (dao/packages.py:1121-1135), and the SQL functions (functions/package_export.sql:27-33). Account scoping is applied at the Assets/AppVersion hop (dao/packages.py:1016-1019, package_export.sql:32-33) — packages themselves are global rows shared across accounts.

base_purl semantics. Package.base_purl is the PURL with version, without qualifiers/subpath (package.py:69-71); qualifiers live on PackageMetadata.purl_qualifiers (package.py:109-113). It is produced by split_purl() (purl_utils.py:11-57), which round-trips through packageurl.PackageURL — so parseable PURLs are stored in packageurl-python's canonical form. Verified against the pinned lib (packageurl-python 0.17.6, poetry.lock:2498-2506): pkg:pypi/Django → pkg:pypi/django, pkg:pypi/typing_extensions → pkg:pypi/typing-extensions, pkg:npm/LeftPad → pkg:npm/leftpad, golang case preserved (github.com/Sirupsen/logrus unchanged). Unparseable strings fall back verbatim (purl_utils.py:24-25), and base_purl may be NULL (package.py:50-54).

The precedent junction. PackageVulnerability (vulnerability_scan.py:455-521) keys on (package_metadata_id, vulnerability_id, distro_id, child_metadata_id), stores per-match variance (fix_state, fix_versions) on the junction, carries covering/secondary indexes for its read paths (vulnerability_scan.py:506-521), and is maintained by the scan write path. Its created_at is the match-recording time, used as the change fence.

Global vs account-scoped tables. vulnerability_scan.py:44-46 explicitly partitions the model file into "GLOBAL TABLES (no account_name in PK)" (Distro, Provider, Vulnerability, Epss, Kev, CvssSource, VulnerabilityScore, VulnerabilityDbState) and "ACCOUNT-SCOPED TABLES" (vulnerability_scan.py:450-453). The multi-tenancy rule ("all queries MUST filter by account_name", CLAUDE.md) is satisfied at read time by joining the account-scoped hierarchy, never by putting accounts on reference data.

Dataset-state precedent. VulnerabilityDbState (vulnerability_scan.py:427-447): singleton row (CheckConstraint("id = 1")), grype_db_built_at + metadata_loaded_at + provider_metadata JSONB. Scanners compare it to converge (scanner/db_bootstrap.py:108-129).

Atomic-replace precedent. Epss/Kev are wholesale-replaced per feed update (vulnerability_scan.py:126-130), and apply_metadata_update.sql:98-103 documents the concurrency rule: DELETE, not TRUNCATE — the proc runs while API readers hold AccessShareLock; TRUNCATE needs AccessExclusive and deadlocks against reader lock order. MVCC makes DELETE+INSERT in one transaction an atomic version swap from the reader's point of view.

Push detection + fanout precedent. data_syncer driver calls notify_feed_update() (v5 data_syncer/drivers/vulnerabilities/vulnerability_db_driver.py:75) → NG POST /notify/feed-update creates the workflow (controllers/notify.py:133-148). The 4-step workflow is registered at jobs/feed_update_workflow.py:491-499 (diff → rescan → events → stale-policy). Per-app events resolve affected versions via get_app_versions_for_scan_units (feed_update_workflow.py:294, 393); policy staleness via queue_policy_reevaluation (feed_update_workflow.py:411).

Ingest hook. SBOM ingest bulk-inserts packages at jobs/sbom_base.py:311 → bulk_add_packages_with_metadata, which stamps resolved pkg_id onto every PreparedPackage (dao/packages.py:374-376) — the exact ID list a resolver needs is already in hand at that point.

Policy gap. policy/gates/ contains only vulnerabilities.py (VulnerabilitiesGate, policy/gates/vulnerabilities.py:786). A PackagesGate must be created for EOL policy (30k-view S8-F).

API conventions in force. Packages are addressed by tuple, not id (api/models/packages.py:2-9); the current row model is PackageResponse{name, version, type, purl, licenses} (api/models/packages.py:55-64); pagination envelope is PaginationInfo{cursor, next_cursor, item_count} (common/models/pagination.py:4-15); summary endpoints exist as GET + filtered POST pairs (controllers/packages.py:73-112); search filters are FilterCondition lists validated against FieldConfig maps (dao/packages.py:1071-1080); single-package addressing by query params is the assets-by-package precedent (controllers/packages.py:125-141). Enums shared by DB and API live in db_entities/enums.py as StrEnum (enums.py:12,33,...).

1. UI → API trace

1.1 Element-by-element map (from the three boards)

UI element (board) Data needed Served by
Status pill in Package Findings rows — Active/EOL/DNE, compact + "since " variants (29634) per-package status, optional status_since Endpoint A: insights.status on each list row
Version-lag pill in Insights column — 0 / <5 / 5-10 / >10 (29633) per-package version_lag int + bucket Endpoint A: insights.version_lag, insights.version_lag_bucket
"Package Status" metric bar (Summary + Contents tabs, 29634/29633) counts by status for the app version Endpoint B: by_status
"EOL Packages" metric bar (Summary tab, 29634) EOL count (subset of by_status) Endpoint B: by_status.EOL
"Version Lag" metric bar (Contents tab, 29633) counts by lag bucket Endpoint B: by_version_lag
Package Status multi-select filter + EOL true/false toggle (29634) filter list rows by status Endpoint C: filter[package_status] on A; package_status field on packages-search
Version Lag filter (29633) filter by bucket Endpoint C: filter[version_lag]
Side panel on row click — Status, Age, Staleness, Avg vuln fix time, Version Lag, Release gap, each with value + explanation; risk ring (30868) full metric set + definitions + provenance for ONE package Endpoint D: package-insights detail
Risk score column + ring (29633/30868, long-term) composite score Out of MVP (O15); reserved optional field on A and D

Board-driven data notes: the "since May 2025" pill variant needs a status_since date that the POC dataset does not produce (SPEC §3.1 metrics have no eol/dne dates) — see O23. "Age" = now − time.first_seen; "Staleness" = now − time.latest_activity; "Avg vuln fix time" maps to time.vuln_fix, which SPEC §4 declares a placeholder — see O24. "Release gap" needs at least the two most recent release dates — needs the timeline decision (O4/O18).

1.2 Response shape — Zach's constraint applied

Insights ride each package row as a small object with status (and version lag) pulled out first-class (they drive tokens, filters, indexes, policy) and everything else as a data-driven metrics: [{metric, value}] array passed through from the dataset — a new metric added to the dataset appears in API responses with zero NG code change. Definitions/labels for rendering come from a metric_registry shipped in the dataset meta (also data-driven), surfaced on the detail endpoint and the summary's dataset block.

New models (api/models/packages.py, names per repo conventions; enums in db_entities/enums.py since they're shared with the DB layer):

class PackageInsightStatus(enum.StrEnum):        # db_entities/enums.py
    ACTIVE = "active"; EOL = "eol"; DNE = "dne"
    UNKNOWN = "unknown"          # project matched, eol/dne inconclusive (SPEC: eol may be null)
    UNANALYZED = "unanalyzed"    # no dataset match / no usable purl (O19 bucket)

class VersionLagBucket(enum.StrEnum):
    CURRENT = "current"                 # 0 behind
    BEHIND_LT_5 = "behind_lt_5"
    BEHIND_5_TO_10 = "behind_5_to_10"
    BEHIND_GT_10 = "behind_gt_10"
    UNKNOWN = "unknown"                 # no match, or version not found in release list

class PackageInsightMetric(BaseModel):
    metric: str                          # e.g. "time.latest_release", "quantitative.open_issues_count"
    value: str | int | float | bool | None

class PackageInsights(BaseModel):        # embedded on list rows
    status: PackageInsightStatus
    status_since: datetime | None = None            # O23 — null until dataset carries it
    version_lag: int | None = None
    version_lag_bucket: VersionLagBucket
    metrics: list[PackageInsightMetric] = []        # data-driven pass-through

class PackageResponse(BaseModel):        # EXTENDED (packages.py:55-64)
    name: str; version: str; type: str
    purl: str | None = None
    licenses: list[LicenseResponse] = []
    insights: PackageInsights | None = None         # None when feature/entitlement off

insights: null (feature off) vs status: UNANALYZED (feature on, no data) are deliberately distinct — the UI hides the column entirely in the first case (S8-E FeatureMap gating) and shows the O19 bucket in the second. [assessment] Inline-always beats ?include=insights (O14): the block is ~150 bytes/row, the join is a PK probe (§3), and the default Contents view needs the status pill — an opt-in include would just be a flag every client always sets.

1.3 Endpoint A — packages list with insights

GET /v2/apps/{app_id}/versions/{version_id}/packages (extend existing, controllers/packages.py:44-70; DAO dao/packages.py:981-1068).

# dao/packages.py — list_packages_for_app_version, outer query extended
rep = (...)                                  # unchanged rep subquery, packages.py:1005-1026
query = (
    select(rep.c.pm_id, rep.c.purl_qualifiers,
           Package.id, Package.name, Package.version, Package.type, Package.base_purl,
           PackageInsightsRow.status, PackageInsightsRow.version_lag,
           PackageInsightsRow.version_lag_bucket, PackageInsightsRow.metrics_cache)
    .select_from(rep)
    .join(Package, Package.id == rep.c.pkg_id)
    .outerjoin(PackageInsightsRow, PackageInsightsRow.package_id == rep.c.pkg_id)   # PK probe
)
if f := filters.get("package_status"):       # Endpoint C, GET-param form
    query = query.where(func.coalesce(PackageInsightsRow.status, "unanalyzed").in_(f))
if f := filters.get("version_lag"):
    query = query.where(func.coalesce(PackageInsightsRow.version_lag_bucket, "unknown").in_(f))
# cursor/order/limit unchanged (pm_id keyset, packages.py:1042-1052)

SQL shape: existing 5-table chain scan for the app version (100–5k rows) + one LEFT JOIN on package_insights.package_id (PK) per row. No new sort orders; keyset pagination untouched (filter columns aren't sort keys, so cursors stay valid under the existing pm_id DESC order).

1.4 Endpoint B — insights summary (metric bars)

New sibling of packages-summary (controllers/packages.py:73-90), M4 sub-resource style:

GET /v2/apps/{app_id}/versions/{version_id}/packages-insights-summary (plus POST variant accepting PackagesSummaryRequest filters later, mirroring controllers/packages.py:93-112 — not in first cut).

class PackagesInsightsSummaryResponse(BaseModel):
    total: int
    by_status: dict[PackageInsightStatus, int]        # zero-filled, stable key set
    by_version_lag: dict[VersionLagBucket, int]
    dataset: InsightsDatasetInfo                       # {generated_at, loaded_at, schema_version}

-- one pass, both dimensions
WITH pkgs AS (                                   -- same chain as packages-summary CTE
    SELECT DISTINCT p.id                          -- grain: Package.id, matches packages-summary
    FROM component_catalog_packages p
    JOIN component_catalog_package_metadata pm  ON pm.package_id = p.id
    JOIN component_catalog_artifact_packages ap ON ap.package_metadata_id = pm.id
    JOIN component_catalog_artifacts art        ON art.uuid = ap.artifact_uuid
    JOIN component_catalog_assets a             ON a.artifact_uuid = art.uuid
    WHERE a.account_name = :account AND a.app_version_uuid = :version
)
SELECT COALESCE(pi.status, 'unanalyzed')            AS status,
       COALESCE(pi.version_lag_bucket, 'unknown')   AS lag_bucket,
       COUNT(*)                                     AS n
FROM pkgs LEFT JOIN component_catalog_package_insights pi ON pi.package_id = pkgs.id
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((1), (2));

Grain note [assessment]: counts are per Package.id, consistent with packages-summary (dao/packages.py:960-966, which counts the GROUP BY Package.id CTE). The list endpoint dedups by (package, qualifiers) (dao/packages.py:991-993) so a qualifier-variant package can show 2 rows but count once — that mismatch exists today between /packages and /packages-summary; do not fix it inside this feature. Insights are per-Package, so per-Package counting is also the truthful grain. Rollups are computed at query time, not precomputed (O11): the query is one indexed chain scan + PK joins over ≤5k rows — same cost class as the existing packages-summary.

1.5 Endpoint C — filtering

Two surfaces, matching S8-C:

  1. GET list params (M4 org convention ?filter[field]=value): filter[package_status]=eol,dne and filter[version_lag]=behind_gt_10 on Endpoint A (WHERE clauses shown in §1.3). Values are the StrEnum wire values; unknown value → 422 with the standard error shape.
  2. packages-search (controllers/packages_search.py:35-72): add virtual fields to PACKAGE_SEARCH_FIELDS (dao/packages.py:1071-1080) the way asset_count is added (dao/packages.py:1159-1164):
field_config["package_status"] = FieldConfig(
    column=func.coalesce(PackageInsightsRow.status, literal("unanalyzed")),
    type="string", allowed_operators=frozenset({FilterOperator.EQ, FilterOperator.IN}))
field_config["version_lag"] = FieldConfig(
    column=PackageInsightsRow.version_lag, type="int", allowed_operators=INT_OPS)
# query gains: .outerjoin(PackageInsightsRow, PackageInsightsRow.package_id == Package.id)

Search tokens already serialize filters (IntSearchToken, dao/packages.py:1245), so paging a status-filtered search works unchanged.

1.6 Endpoint D — per-package insights detail (side panel)

Packages have no API id (api/models/packages.py:2-9); the addressing precedent is query params (assets-by-package, controllers/packages.py:125-141):

GET /v2/apps/{app_id}/versions/{version_id}/package-insights?name=&version=&type=[&purl=]

class PackageInsightDetail(BaseModel):
    metric: str
    value: str | int | float | bool | None
    label: str | None = None          # from dataset metric_registry
    definition: str | None = None     # from dataset metric_registry
    provenance: list[str] = []        # source ids, from dataset per-metric provenance

class PackageInsightsDetailResponse(BaseModel):
    name: str; version: str; type: str; purl: str | None
    status: PackageInsightStatus
    status_since: datetime | None = None
    version_lag: int | None; version_lag_bucket: VersionLagBucket
    latest_version: str | None                    # for "5.5.5.5 → 6.1.0" rendering
    insights: list[PackageInsightDetail]          # Age/Staleness/…: derived server-side, see below
    releases: list[ReleaseEntry] | None = None    # [{version, date}] newest-first, if O4=yes
    risk: RiskScore | None = None                 # reserved, O15
    dataset: InsightsDatasetInfo

Query shape: resolve (name, version, type) → Package.id within the app-version scope (reuse the parse_namespace/list_assets_with_package lookup pattern, dao/packages.py:1282-1381), then package_insights PK probe + oss_projects PK probe for the full record (releases, provenance). Derived side-panel values (age_days, staleness_days, release_gap_days) are computed in the DAO from the time metrics — they're presentation-derived, not stored, so "now"-relative values are always fresh. They're emitted as entries in the same insights array (metric names derived.age_days etc.) so the panel is fully data-driven too.

2. Enterprise Postgres schema

Two new tables + one state singleton, all in enterprise/services/component_catalog/db_entities/ (new file oss_insights.py). All three are GLOBAL tables in the documented sense of vulnerability_scan.py:44-46 — no account_name. The multi-tenancy rule is honored exactly as the vuln tables honor it: no read path ever queries them except through the account-scoped app-version chain (§1 queries all start from Assets.account_name = :account), and the tables contain only public upstream facts about public OSS projects — nothing customer-derived. This is the same posture as Epss, Kev, Vulnerability (vulnerability_scan.py:121-192, 252).

2.1 component_catalog_oss_projects — the dataset mirror

One row per project, keyed by canonical version-less purl. Replaced wholesale per dataset version (§5). No FKs point at it and it points at nothing — the same "no FK — those tables are truncated+reloaded" rule as Vulnerability.cve_id → Epss/Kev (vulnerability_scan.py:271-273).

class OssProject(Base):
    __tablename__ = "component_catalog_oss_projects"

    purl: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, primary_key=True)   # canonical, version-less (O10 spec)
    # First-class, typed: the closed-set / filterable / policy-relevant facts.
    status: Mapped[PackageInsightStatus] = mapped_column(pg_enum(PackageInsightStatus, "package_insight_status"))
    eol: Mapped[bool | None]                    # SPEC metrics.boolean.eol (nullable per SPEC §4)
    dne: Mapped[bool]                           # SPEC metrics.boolean.dne
    latest_version: Mapped[str | None]          # releases.latest — drives version-lag + "→ 6.1.0" UI
    first_seen: Mapped[datetime | None]
    latest_release: Mapped[datetime | None]
    latest_activity: Mapped[datetime | None]
    vuln_fix: Mapped[datetime | None]
    # Extensible: everything else, verbatim from the dataset (Zach constraint).
    metrics: Mapped[list[dict[str, Any]]] = mapped_column(JSONB)        # [{metric, value}, ...]
    provenance: Mapped[dict[str, Any] | None] = mapped_column(JSONB(none_as_null=True), default=None)
    releases: Mapped[list[dict[str, Any]] | None] = mapped_column(JSONB(none_as_null=True), default=None)
                                                # [{version, date}] newest-first, capped (O4)
    record_hash: Mapped[str]                    # dataset-computed canonical hash; differ key (§4)
    generated_at: Mapped[datetime]              # per-record generated_at from dataset

    # PK index on purl is the only index needed: every consumer arrives by purl equality.

Column strategy — decided: hybrid, and here is the defense. Three candidates:

  • Pure JSONB metrics column: maximally extensible, but status filtering/counting and the PackagesGate would run metrics @> ... or ->> extraction inside the hot per-app-version queries, need GIN/expression indexes with awkward enum semantics, and lose type/enum safety in the OpenAPI schema. Rejected.
  • Pure typed columns / metric-rows table (EAV): metric-rows (one row per (purl, metric)) makes every read a pivot, multiplies row count by ~12×, and still doesn't give indexed status filtering without special-casing. All-typed-columns means every new dataset metric is a migration + code change — exactly what Zach's constraint forbids. Rejected.
  • Hybrid (chosen): the closed, product-committed set — status, eol/dne, latest_version, the four time metrics — as typed columns (they feed tokens, filters, buckets, policy, and the four-date side panel); everything else rides the metrics JSONB array untouched. A future metric ships in the dataset → appears in metrics → appears in API insights.metrics and the detail panel with registry-provided label/definition, no NG release. If a future metric needs filtering, that is the moment it gets promoted to a typed column via a normal migration — filterability is precisely the property that justifies schema. This mirrors how the repo already treats vuln data: typed columns for what queries touch, JSONB for payload (fix_versions JSONB on the junction, vulnerability_scan.py:503; cvss_assessments JSONB on VulnerabilityScore, vulnerability_scan.py:416-418).

Note the filtering/index requirement lands on package_insights (§2.2), not here — per-app-version status filtering never scans oss_projects by status.

2.2 component_catalog_package_insights — the per-package resolution table

The junction (§3 defends its existence). One row per packages row — including unmatched and purl-less packages — written by the shared resolver. FK CASCADE from packages so GC of a Package (GcQuarantineMixin, package.py:42) cleans it up without a new collector.

class PackageInsightsRow(Base):                      # class name avoids clash with API model
    __tablename__ = "component_catalog_package_insights"

    package_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        BigInteger, ForeignKey("component_catalog_packages.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        primary_key=True)
    # Normalized version-less purl computed from Package at resolve time.
    # NULL when base_purl is NULL or unparseable. Kept even when unmatched —
    # it is the reverse-lookup key for dataset-refresh re-resolution (§3.3, §5).
    versionless_purl: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)
    # NULL = no dataset match. No FK to oss_projects (wholesale-replaced; Vulnerability.cve_id
    # precedent, vulnerability_scan.py:271-273).
    project_purl: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)
    # Denormalized + package-derived facts, so list/summary/policy never touch oss_projects:
    status: Mapped[PackageInsightStatus] = mapped_column(
        pg_enum(PackageInsightStatus, "package_insight_status"),
        default=PackageInsightStatus.UNANALYZED)
    version_lag: Mapped[int | None]                  # releases newer than Package.version; NULL unknown
    version_lag_bucket: Mapped[VersionLagBucket] = mapped_column(
        pg_enum(VersionLagBucket, "version_lag_bucket"), default=VersionLagBucket.UNKNOWN)
    resolved_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(default=anchore_now_datetime)
    dataset_generated_at: Mapped[datetime | None]    # which dataset version produced this row

    __table_args__ = (
        # Refresh path: changed purls -> affected package rows (§5). Partial: skip purl-less rows.
        Index(truncate_index_name("ix_pkg_insights_versionless_purl"),
              "versionless_purl",
              postgresql_where=text("versionless_purl IS NOT NULL")),
    )

Index decisions. (1) PK on package_id serves every API/policy read — reads are always app-version-scoped first (the selective predicate), then PK-probe this table; a bare status index would never win over that plan for per-version queries, so it is deliberately absent. (2) versionless_purl partial index serves the refresh translator (changed purls → package_ids) and covers previously unmatched packages when a new dataset adds a project (§3.3). If a future "all EOL packages across my account" report appears, add a partial index (status) WHERE status IN ('eol','dne') then — not speculatively.

Version-lag derivation [assessment]: version_lag = count of releases in the project's release list strictly newer than the package's version, computed in Python by the resolver with an ecosystem-aware comparator (O25); bucket thresholds per board 29633: 0 → CURRENT, 1–4 → BEHIND_LT_5, 5–10 → BEHIND_5_TO_10, >10 → BEHIND_GT_10. It lives here (not on oss_projects) because it is a (package version × project) fact, not a project fact — the single strongest structural argument for this table's existence.

Status derivation (loader/resolver, single place): dne is true → DNE; else eol is true → EOL; else eol is false → ACTIVE; else matched-but-null → UNKNOWN; no match / no purl → UNANALYZED. (O23 covers whether ETL should pre-derive this in the dataset instead.)

2.3 component_catalog_oss_insights_db_state — dataset bookkeeping

Mirror of VulnerabilityDbState (vulnerability_scan.py:427-447):

class OssInsightsDbState(Base):
    __tablename__ = "component_catalog_oss_insights_db_state"
    __table_args__ = (CheckConstraint("id = 1", name="oss_insights_db_state_singleton"),)

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True, default=1)
    dataset_checksum: Mapped[str | None]         # data_syncer record checksum — debounce key
    dataset_generated_at: Mapped[datetime | None]
    dataset_schema_version: Mapped[str | None]   # sqlite meta.schema_version (§4.3)
    loaded_at: Mapped[datetime | None]
    record_count: Mapped[int | None]
    metric_registry: Mapped[dict[str, Any]] = mapped_column(
        JSONB, nullable=False, server_default=text("'{}'::jsonb"))   # labels/definitions for D

dataset_checksum is the ensure_ready-style debounce (feed-update-analysis: checksum-vs-PG-state); for a non-scanner layer the check happens at workflow start, not per-scan.

2.4 Migrations & conventions checklist

All three tables are new, so Base.metadata.create_all() (run by run_ng_enterprise_migration around each version step, per repo CLAUDE.md) creates them — including the two pg_enum types — with no hand-written DDL. Register the release's upgrade_60XX.py entry in migrations/registry.py regardless (bookkeeping + the version gate); its body can be a no-op for shape. No existing table is altered — deliberately: the design adds zero columns to component_catalog_packages (no backfill over the largest table in the schema). Index names pass truncate_index_name (package.py:32, naming.py); JSONB not JSON; enums are StrEnum + pg_enum per db_entities/enums.py:12ff; if any later change alters these tables, it goes through migrations/utils.py helpers (add_column/add_index/…, utils.py:170-345) with idempotent guards.

3. The junction question — answered

Decision: (b) a resolution table (package_insights, §2.2), maintained by one shared idempotent resolver. But note what it is not: it is not a many-to-many junction like PackageVulnerability — it's a 1:0..1 sidecar keyed by package_id that materializes the join normalize(packages.base_purl) → oss_projects.purl plus the package-version-dependent derivations.

3.1 Why not (a) direct join on purl

The direct join packages.base_purl = package_insights.purl doesn't even typecheck semantically: base_purl contains the version (package.py:69-71, e.g. pkg:pypi/django@4.2) while insights are per-project (SPEC: record keyed by unversioned purl; 30k-view S2). The join would be strip_version(base_purl) = oss_projects.purl, i.e. an expression like regexp_replace(base_purl, '@[^@/]*$', '') on the packages side — needing an expression index on a shared hot table, or 5k per-row regexp evaluations per listing. Feasible, but then:

  1. Normalization mismatches become permanent, silent misses. NG's base_purl is canonical for the packageurl-python version that wrote the row (purl_utils.py:23-34). 0.17.6 lowercases pypi/npm names and folds pypi _→- (verified §0); the dependency floor is >=0.11,<2 (pyproject.toml:53), so historical rows may predate a normalization rule, and unparseable purls are stored verbatim (purl_utils.py:24-25). The capital-D-Django class of bug is exactly a raw-SQL-equality casualty: pkg:pypi/Django@... written under an older normalizer never matches dataset pkg:pypi/django, and with a pure SQL join there is no code point to apply a retry/fold — you'd have to rewrite packages rows (immutable, deduped, shared across accounts — a rewrite risks unique-constraint collisions on package_unique_key, package.py:76-84). With a resolver, normalization runs in Python at match time, can case-fold/underscore-fold per ecosystem rules, and a normalizer upgrade is fixed by re-running the resolver — no data surgery.
  2. Version lag is not computable in the join. It needs the package's version located inside the project's ordered release list under ecosystem version semantics (PEP440 vs semver vs epochs). That is a Python computation per (package, project) pair; doing it per-request per-row is waste, so it must be materialized somewhere keyed by package_id — at which point the resolution table exists anyway and denormalizing status into it is free.
  3. Filter/index needs. filter[package_status] and the summary GROUP BY want an indexed, typed column reachable from the app-version chain. Via (a) that's an expression join then a status lookup on oss_projects per row; via (b) it's a PK probe on a 5-column row.

3.2 Query-cost comparison (app-version listing, 100–5k packages)

  • (a) direct join: chain scan (unchanged) + per-row regexp_replace + index probe on oss_projects.purl (60-byte text key, 0.1–5M-row index) + status fetch. ~2 index descents/row plus expression eval; and version-lag simply unavailable. [assessment] ~1.5–3× the added cost of (b), all in the hot path, correctness caveats above.
  • (b) resolution table: chain scan + LEFT JOIN PK probe on package_insights (int8 key, narrow row) — the cheapest join Postgres does; oss_projects untouched at list time. Summary = same + GROUP BY over ≤5k rows. [assessment] added cost is ~1 buffer hit per row; on 5k rows, low single-digit ms.

Both are viable for the list query; (a) loses on version lag, normalization repair, and filter indexing. The cost of (b) is the maintenance obligation — addressed by making one resolver serve every trigger:

3.3 The shared resolver — one idempotent function, three triggers

async def resolve_insights_for_packages(
    session, *,
    package_ids: Iterable[int] | None = None,     # trigger 1: SBOM ingest (new/updated pkg ids)
    changed_purls: Iterable[str] | None = None,   # trigger 2: dataset refresh (differ output)
) -> list[int]:                                   # returns package_ids whose DERIVED row changed
    """Both None => full re-resolve (trigger 3: first load, schema bump, rollback)."""

    if package_ids is None:
        if changed_purls is not None:
            # Reverse lookup via the resolution table itself. Because UNMATCHED packages
            # still carry versionless_purl (§2.2), a NEW project appearing in the dataset
            # re-resolves the packages that were waiting for it — no scan of `packages`.
            package_ids = await session.scalars(
                select(PackageInsightsRow.package_id)
                .where(PackageInsightsRow.versionless_purl.in_(changed_purls)))   # partial idx
        else:
            package_ids = await session.scalars(select(Package.id).where(Package.id != 0))

    changed: list[int] = []
    for batch in batched(package_ids, 1000):                      # dao/packages.py:264-273 limits
        pkgs = (await session.execute(
            select(Package.id, Package.name, Package.version, Package.type, Package.base_purl)
            .where(Package.id.in_(batch)))).all()

        keyed = {p.id: normalize_versionless_purl(p) for p in pkgs}
        #   normalize_versionless_purl: packageurl canonical form, version stripped,
        #   ecosystem folds (pypi lower+underscore, npm lower, golang case-preserving),
        #   syft-type -> purl-type mapping for purl-less rows where derivable; None otherwise.
        #   THE O10 contract: identical function (spec'd + conformance-tested) runs in dataset ETL.

        projects = {r.purl: r for r in await session.execute(
            select(OssProject).where(OssProject.purl.in_({k for k in keyed.values() if k})))}

        rows = [derive_insights_row(p, keyed[p.id], projects.get(keyed[p.id])) for p in pkgs]
        #   derive_insights_row: status per §2.2 rule; version_lag = count of project.releases
        #   strictly newer than p.version under ecosystem comparator; bucket per board thresholds.

        stmt = (pg_insert(PackageInsightsRow).values(rows)
                .on_conflict_do_update(index_elements=["package_id"], set_=EXCLUDED_ALL)
                # no-op-skip so `changed` is truthful and refresh events don't over-fire:
                .where(PackageInsightsRow.__table__.c != excluded)   # IS DISTINCT FROM row-compare
                .returning(PackageInsightsRow.package_id))
        changed += list(await session.scalars(stmt))
    return changed

Idempotent by construction: output is a pure function of current (packages, oss_projects) state, applied as an upsert. Re-runs converge; the ingest trigger racing the refresh trigger computes identical rows. Trigger points:

  1. Initialization — end of SBOM ingest, right after bulk_add_packages_with_metadata (jobs/sbom_base.py:311); the PreparedPackage.pkg_ids are already stamped (dao/packages.py:374-376). Runs even when the artifact already existed only for pkg rows lacking an insights row (cheap anti-join guard). If the insights dataset isn't loaded yet (state row empty), rows are written as UNANALYZED with versionless_purl populated — first dataset load's full re-resolve (trigger 3) upgrades them. [assessment] run it in the same ingest job as a post-step (~ms per SBOM at batch sizes here), not a separate job — O26.
  2. Maintenance — dataset refresh workflow (§5) passes the differ's changed purls.
  3. Recovery/first-load — full re-resolve.

The triggers differ, the resolver is shared — requirement met.

4. Middleware: the sqlite dataset

4.1 Schema (wire format, published by EDS, pulled by data_syncer)

-- meta: single-table key/value, like grype-db style provenance
CREATE TABLE meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL);
-- required keys: schema_version ("1.0"), generated_at (RFC3339), record_count,
--                purl_normalization_version (O10 contract version),
--                metric_registry (JSON: [{metric, label, definition, unit, kind}, ...])

CREATE TABLE oss_projects (
    purl            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,   -- canonical version-less purl (O10)
    status          TEXT,               -- optional pre-derived; NG loader may recompute (O23)
    eol             INTEGER,            -- 0/1/NULL
    dne             INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- 0/1
    latest_version  TEXT,
    first_seen      TEXT,               -- YYYY-MM-DD (SPEC date format)
    latest_release  TEXT,
    latest_activity TEXT,
    vuln_fix        TEXT,
    metrics         TEXT NOT NULL,      -- JSON [{metric, value}] — full SPEC metric set, verbatim
    provenance      TEXT,               -- JSON per-metric source ids
    releases        TEXT,               -- JSON [{version, date}] newest-first, CAPPED (see 4.4/O4)
    record_hash     TEXT NOT NULL       -- sha256 of canonical row serialization, computed by ETL
);
-- no secondary indexes: consumers do PK lookups + full scans only

4.2 Mirror-exactly vs neutral — decided: near-mirror with a typed transform loader

A byte-for-byte mirror with ATTACH + INSERT...SELECT is not actually attainable: PG has enum types, timestamptz, JSONB, and postgres_fdw/sqlite-attach isn't in the deployment picture — the loader is a Python read-batch-insert either way (that is exactly how the vuln layer works: sqlite streamed from the object store, imported, scanner/db_bootstrap.py:57-129). So the real question is schema shape coupling, and there the answer is: keep the shapes deliberately congruent (column names/meanings 1:1 with §2.1) so the loader is a dumb typed copy (~50 lines), but treat the sqlite schema as a versioned public contract, not an implementation detail:

  • meta.schema_version is MAJOR.MINOR. Loader accepts equal MAJOR, logs+ignores unknown columns (MINOR additions = new metrics/columns), refuses unknown MAJOR: leaves PG state untouched, emits an operator-visible event. The state row records what was loaded (§2.3).
  • Additive-only within a MAJOR; column removals/renames/semantic changes bump MAJOR and require an NG release that understands both for one overlap cycle.
  • "Exactly one consumer" makes tight coupling acceptable today but the discipline costs nothing and is what lets anchorectl/airgap tooling or a second consumer (v5? UI export?) appear later without archaeology. [assessment]

The extensibility story stays intact under near-mirroring because new metrics ship inside the metrics JSON column, not as new sqlite columns — a dataset with three new metrics is a MINOR bump the existing loader passes through untouched.

4.3 Diff story

The dataset is a primary-key table with a per-row content hash, so the generic differ from the metadata-layer plan (feed-update-analysis §"What is vulnerability-specific" item 1) is:

-- differ(old.sqlite, new.sqlite) -> stream of changed identity keys (purls)
SELECT n.purl FROM new.oss_projects n
LEFT JOIN old.oss_projects o USING (purl)
WHERE o.purl IS NULL OR o.record_hash != n.record_hash     -- added + modified
UNION ALL
SELECT o.purl FROM old.oss_projects o
LEFT JOIN new.oss_projects n USING (purl)
WHERE n.purl IS NULL;                                       -- removed

Streamed (no materialization), mirroring streaming_db_diff. record_hash must be a canonical serialization hash computed by ETL (O30): hash stability is what keeps "changed" honest — non-semantic serialization churn (key ordering, float formatting) would otherwise re-fire the whole pipeline every publish. First load (no old archive): skip diff, full re-resolve.

data_syncer keeps N versions of dataset records in the object store (existing behavior — the vuln differ already fetches old+new), which is also the rollback story: PG holds exactly one version; roll back by re-loading the prior archive (O27).

4.4 Archive size estimates [assessment — order of magnitude]

Per-row payload: purl ~60B, dates/scalars ~80B, metrics JSON ~250B, provenance ~150B, hash 64B ≈ 600B; sqlite overhead ~1.3× ⇒ ~800B/row. Timelines: ~25 releases avg × ~30B JSON ≈ +750B/row (long tail has few releases; head has hundreds — cap at newest 50 to bound it).

Universe (O1) metrics-only sqlite + capped timelines archive (zstd/gz, ~4–6×)
100k projects ~60–80 MB ~140–160 MB ~15 / ~30 MB
1M projects ~0.6–0.8 GB ~1.4–1.6 GB ~150 / ~300 MB
5M projects ~3–4 GB ~7–8 GB ~0.7 / ~1.5 GB

Reference point: grype v6 vuln DB is ~1 GB sqlite / ~200 MB archive. ⇒ 1M with capped timelines is vuln-DB-class and fine through the existing pipe (data_syncer object store, 1GB cache bypass already exists for vuln DB); 5M with timelines is over budget — the O1 universe and O4 timeline decisions are coupled, and the recommendation is: ship capped timelines (they unlock version lag (O18), release gap, and staleness — half the side panel) and hold the universe ≤ ~1M by rank-based selection until there's evidence more is needed.

5. Load + refresh pipeline

The insights layer instantiated against the metadata-layer interface (feed-update-analysis § "Proposed common core"):

oss_insights_layer = MetadataLayer(
    dataset_name="oss_insights_db",
    loader=load_oss_insights,             # below
    differ=generic_pk_differ,             # §4.3 — the default, not custom
    recompute=None,                       # no rescan; the diff IS the change set
    translator=insights_translator,       # purl-keyed, below
    event_factory=ApplicationInsightsUpdated,   # + v5 stub + notifications formatter entry
    policy_relevant=True,                 # gated on PackagesGate existing (S8-F)
)

Detection: data_syncer OssInsightsDriver.load() → notify_dataset_update("oss_insights_db") (the generalized /notify/feed-update, controllers/notify.py:133-148, gaining a dataset-name param) → create_workflow(METADATA_UPDATE, layer=oss_insights). Debounce: workflow start compares data_syncer's latest checksum against oss_insights_db_state.dataset_checksum (§2.3) and no-ops when current — the ensure_ready pattern without the scanner.

# STEP 1 — load + diff
async def handle_insights_load(ctx):
    record = await data_syncer.latest("oss_insights_db")
    if record.checksum == await get_state_checksum():           # debounce / duplicate workflow
        return {"skipped": True}
    new = await stream_from_object_store(record)                # db_bootstrap.py:154-187 pattern
    validate_schema_version(new.meta)                           # §4.2 gate; refuse+event on MAJOR
    old = await fetch_previous_archive_if_any()

    changed_purls = None if old is None else list(generic_pk_differ(old, new))   # §4.3

    async with advisory_lock(META_INSIGHTS):                    # exclusive-phase, like META_VUL
        async with session_scope() as s:                        # ONE tx = atomic version swap
            await s.execute(delete(OssProject))                 # DELETE not TRUNCATE:
                                                                # apply_metadata_update.sql:98-103
            for batch in batched(rows_from_sqlite(new), _BATCH):    # 65535-param law,
                await s.execute(pg_insert(OssProject).values(batch)) # dao/packages.py:239-262
            await upsert_state(s, record.checksum, new.meta)    # checksum,+registry,+counts
    return {"changed_purls": changed_purls}                     # None => full re-resolve

# STEP 2 — resolve (replaces the vuln layer's rescan; trivial middle, as predicted)
async def handle_insights_resolve(ctx):
    changed = ctx.input["changed_purls"]
    affected_pkg_ids = await resolve_insights_for_packages(
        changed_purls=changed) if changed is not None else \
        await resolve_insights_for_packages()                   # §3.3 — same function, trigger 2/3
    return {"changed_package_ids": affected_pkg_ids}            # only rows that ACTUALLY changed

# STEP 3 — translate + events (purl/package_id-keyed translator; the vuln one keys on
# (pm_id, distro_id), feed_update_workflow.py:294 — this is its purl-keyed sibling)
async def handle_insights_events(ctx):
    targets = await session.execute(select(
            AppVersion.account_name, AppVersion.app_uuid, AppVersion.uuid).distinct()
        .select_from(PackageInsightsRow)
        .join(PackageMetadata, PackageMetadata.package_id == PackageInsightsRow.package_id)
        .join(ArtifactPackage, ArtifactPackage.package_metadata_id == PackageMetadata.id)
        .join(Assets, Assets.artifact_uuid == ArtifactPackage.artifact_uuid)
        .join(AppVersion, (AppVersion.uuid == Assets.app_version_uuid)
                          & (AppVersion.account_name == Assets.account_name))
        .where(PackageInsightsRow.package_id.in_(ctx.input["changed_package_ids"])))
    # one ApplicationInsightsUpdated per (account, app), 50-version cap —
    # exact shape of _emit_app_vulnerability_events, feed_update_workflow.py:280-337 (O12: yes, emit)
    return {"targets": targets}

# STEP 4 — stale policy
async def handle_insights_policy(ctx):
    await queue_policy_reevaluation(ctx.input["targets"])       # feed_update_workflow.py:411 — as-is

Workflow registration mirrors feed_update_workflow.py:491-499 with steps load → resolve → events → enqueue-policy-evals.

Swap mechanism — decided: DELETE+INSERT in one transaction. Justification: (i) it is the codified precedent — apply_metadata_update.sql:98-103 chose DELETE over TRUNCATE specifically because readers hold AccessShareLock during the swap, and MVCC gives readers a consistent old-version snapshot until commit; (ii) table-rename swap needs ACCESS EXCLUSIVE anyway, breaks ORM metadata/create_all bookkeeping, and orphans the PK name; (iii) partition-by-dataset-version swap is the right tool only past ~5M rows (WAL for a 1M-row swap is ~1–2 GB, minutes of load — acceptable at daily cadence per O7). Escape hatch if the universe grows: dataset_version column + pointer flip in the state row + lazy delete — a contained refactor. [assessment]

No recompute step exists — confirming feed-update-analysis: the differ output feeds the resolver directly; the expensive vuln machinery (grype pool, DIFF_VALIDATE, scan queues) has no insights analog.

PackagesGate query. The gate (new, policy/gates/packages.py) needs packages of an app-version × insights status to evaluate triggers like package_status in (EOL, DNE) or version_lag > N. Served by an R-style SQL function (pattern of package_export.sql) so policy stays on the SQL-function convention:

CREATE FUNCTION app_version_package_insights(_account_name text, _version_uuid uuid)
RETURNS TABLE (package_id bigint, name text, version text, type text, base_purl text,
               status package_insight_status, version_lag int,
               version_lag_bucket version_lag_bucket, latest_version text,
               eol boolean, dne boolean, latest_release timestamptz)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    WITH pkgs AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.name, p.version, p.type, p.base_purl
        FROM component_catalog_packages p
        JOIN component_catalog_package_metadata pm  ON pm.package_id = p.id
        JOIN component_catalog_artifact_packages ap ON ap.package_metadata_id = pm.id
        JOIN component_catalog_artifacts art        ON art.uuid = ap.artifact_uuid
        JOIN component_catalog_assets a             ON a.artifact_uuid = art.uuid
        WHERE a.account_name = _account_name AND a.app_version_uuid = _version_uuid
    )                                                   -- identical chain: package_export.sql:27-33
    SELECT k.id, k.name, k.version, k.type, k.base_purl,
           COALESCE(pi.status, 'unanalyzed'), pi.version_lag,
           COALESCE(pi.version_lag_bucket, 'unknown'), op.latest_version,
           op.eol, op.dne, op.latest_release
    FROM pkgs k
    LEFT JOIN component_catalog_package_insights pi ON pi.package_id = k.id
    LEFT JOIN component_catalog_oss_projects op     ON op.purl = pi.project_purl;
$$;

One chain scan + two PK-joins — the schema serves the gate with no additional structure, and the same function can back Endpoint D's bulk needs. Policy re-eval only fires usefully once this gate exists (feed-update-analysis item 4); until then step 4 is registered but inert.

6. Cardinality, sizing, load times, and open questions

6.1 Sizing table [assessment — order of magnitude; verify with EXPLAIN/benchmarks before GA]

Object @100k universe @1M universe @5M universe
sqlite archive (see §4.4) 15–30 MB 150–300 MB 0.7–1.5 GB
oss_projects heap (PG, +timelines) ~150 MB ~1.5 GB ~7 GB
oss_projects PK index (text purl) ~15 MB ~150 MB ~700 MB
PG load (DELETE+INSERT, batched) ~10–20 s ~2–5 min ~10–25 min
sqlite diff (hash join on PK) seconds ~10–30 s ~1–3 min
Object @1M packages rows @10M packages rows
package_insights heap (~120 B/row) ~120 MB ~1.2 GB
PK (int8) + versionless_purl partial idx ~25 MB + ~90 MB ~250 MB + ~900 MB
full re-resolve (version-lag in Python, ~5–20k pkg/s) ~1–3 min ~10–30 min
typical refresh re-resolve (≤1% purls changed/day) seconds ~tens of seconds
per-request overhead, list of 5k pkgs (PK LEFT JOIN) ~1–5 ms ~1–5 ms

Full re-resolve happens only on first load / normalizer upgrade / rollback; steady state is the changed-purl subset. Ingest-time resolve is O(packages-in-SBOM) — hundreds of rows, milliseconds, lost in the noise of bulk_add_packages_with_metadata.

6.2 Decisions taken here (recommended, not yet ratified)

D1 hybrid columns+JSONB on oss_projects (§2.1) · D2 resolution table over direct purl join (§3) · D3 one row per package incl. UNMATCHED/UNANALYZED, versionless_purl kept on unmatched rows (§2.2/§3.3) · D4 DELETE+INSERT single-tx swap, single PG version (§5) · D5 near-mirror sqlite + typed transform loader + MAJOR.MINOR schema gate (§4.2) · D6 record_hash in dataset, generic PK differ (§4.3) · D7 insights inline on list rows, no ?include (O14 → resolved here) · D8 rollups query-time, not precomputed (O11 → resolved here, revisit only with evidence) · D9 emit ApplicationInsightsUpdated per (account, app) (O12 → yes) · D10 status enum includes UNKNOWN and UNANALYZED (O16/O19 interface: DNE stays in the enum even if EOL-only ships first — an unused enum value costs nothing; the ETL just never emits it until DNE is on).

6.3 Open questions (existing O-numbers touched, new O23+)

Touched: O1/O4 coupled by sizing (§4.4 — recommend capped timelines, ≤1M universe); O10 the normalization contract is now concrete: one spec'd normalize_versionless_purl function + purl_normalization_version in dataset meta + conformance fixtures run by both ETL and NG (§3.3); O11/O12/O14/O16/O19 resolved as D7–D10 above; O15 risk out of MVP, field slots reserved; O18 version lag requires the release list — answered by shipping capped timelines.

New:

  • O23 — status_since sourcing. The "EOL | since May 2025" pill variant has no backing datum: SPEC metrics carry no eol/dne dates (deps.dev isDeprecated is undated; GitHub archived_at is fetchable but not collected). Options: add eol_since to the dataset (ETL work), proxy with latest_activity (dishonest), or ship the pill without the date variant first. Also: who owns status derivation — ETL (status column pre-derived, changes ship datasetly) vs NG loader (§2.2 rule)? Recommend ETL derives, NG validates. Product + data-team decision.
  • O24 — vuln_fix metric quality. SPEC §4 marks it a placeholder (latest_release when advisoryKeys non-empty). The side panel labels it "Avg vulnerability fix time" — shipping a placeholder under that label misleads. Either real advisory→fix resolution lands in S1, or the panel drops the row until it does.
  • O25 — version comparator ownership. version_lag needs per-ecosystem version ordering (PEP440, semver, maven, distro epochs). Which library (packaging / univers / custom), where the per-type dispatch lives, and behavior when the package's version isn't in the release list at all (private fork/pre-release → UNKNOWN bucket?).
  • O26 — resolver-at-ingest execution point. Same-job post-step (recommended, §3.3) vs a queued follow-up job; interacts with SBOM ingest latency SLO and with whether UNANALYZED rows are acceptable for a few seconds after upload.
  • O27 — rollback contract. PG keeps one dataset version; rollback = re-load prior archive from data_syncer's retained records + full re-resolve. Confirm data_syncer retention ≥2 for oss_insights_db and that "keep N-1" (30k-view S7) means archives, not PG tables.
  • O28 — summary/count grain. Insights counts are per Package.id; the list dedups per (package, qualifiers) (dao/packages.py:991-993 vs 960-966). Tolerated mismatch today — decide whether the UI's "#" chips must equal visible row counts exactly.
  • O29 — sentinel row. Package.id = 0 sentinel (dao/packages.py:100-114) must be excluded from resolution (§3.3 does) and from summary counts — trivially handled, recorded so it isn't forgotten.
  • O30 — record_hash canonicalization. ETL must hash a canonical serialization (sorted keys, fixed date/float formats) or every publish diffs as 100% changed. Needs a written rule in the dataset spec + a "diff of identical inputs is empty" CI check.
  • O31 — deleted projects. When a purl leaves the dataset (universe shrink), affected packages fall back to UNANALYZED via the resolver (project lookup misses). Confirm that's the wanted UX vs. retaining last-known insights with a staleness marker — interacts with O1 universe churn.

README states code was "largely produced with code gen tools" to support a rapid prototype -> PM demo -> customer feedback loop. Containerized 4-project pipeline: - purlify_sbom: Syft JSON SBOM -> deduplicated project-level PURLs (strips versions/qualifiers, normalizes forge URLs, npm nesting/public-private detection). - purl_summarize_depsdev: deps.dev metadata/advisories/scorecards per PURL. Metrics: boolean dne/eol; time first_seen/latest_release/vuln_fix/latest_activity; qualitative active (release <365d), maintained (activity <730d and not EOL), popular (scorecard >=5 or stars >=100). npm/PyPI/Go/Maven/Cargo/RubyGems/NuGet. - hattrick: configurable record-scoring library (weight strategies linear/equal/slow_decay/fast_decay). OSSRiskScorer ranks by: dne, eol, project newness, release staleness, vuln fix time. - oss_insights: FastAPI+SQLite web dashboard (SBOM upload, risk-ranked global view, per-SBOM categorization, package detail, PURL overrides, read-only mode).

3. oss_insights_poc/alpha_stack/ — spec-driven rebuild (ACTIVE: commits 2026-07-09/10/12)

  • make_oss_identifiers ("oss-identifiers"): flexible input (PURL, owner/repo, RPM filename, registry URL, name) -> canonical resolution envelope {record, meta, health}: purl, source_code_url, registry_url, confidence, per-probe provenance. SPEC.md is the source of truth; >=19 ecosystems; iterative multi-source corroboration; live URL verification; stateless. Repo contains CLAUDE.md and an IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md written so "a coding agent can reproduce the project from an empty directory".
  • make_oss_insight ("oss-insight"): enriches a resolved identifier -> release timeline {version,date} + metrics (boolean incl. dne/eol, time, qualitative, quantitative). deps.dev primary; fallback reconciliation from native registry, Go module proxy, forge Releases, ecosyste.ms. OS-distro package types (rpm/deb/apk) explicitly out of scope — separate pipeline.

Validation experiments (make_oss_insight)

  • Experiment 0 (completed 2026-07-10): 12,055 PURLs = 7,000 curated (ecosyste.ms 500 most-downloaded x 14 ecosystems) + 5,055 net-new from DockerHub official-image SBOMs via syft 1.46.0. Any-enrichment 91% overall; 99% curated, 80% sbom (gap dominated by runtime-internal artifacts that are not published registry packages). Recall/breadth only.
  • Experiment 1 (completed 2026-07-11): 713 PURLs (629 real stratified popular/mid/tail x 14 ecosystems + 84 verified-404 fakes) validated against ground-truth oracle captured from ecosyste.ms at build time. Any enrichment 620/629 (99%); dne false-positives 8/629 (1%); fake rejection 84/84 (100%); source_code_url precision 520/542 (96%); releases.latest agreement 501/605 (83%); timeline completeness >=90% for 588/611 (96%). Wall time 150 min at concurrency 3.

External data sources (defaults from oss-identifiers SPEC §13 + oss-insight README)

  1. deps.dev v3alpha (api.deps.dev) — purl lookup, project package-versions
  2. ecosyste.ms packages API (packages.ecosyste.ms) — registry package lookup; also the experiment corpus + validation oracle
  3. ecosyste.ms repos API (repos.ecosyste.ms) — repository lookup by URL
  4. ClearlyDefined (api.clearlydefined.io)
  5. public.purldb.io
  6. GitHub API (optional GITHUB_TOKEN), GitLab API, Bitbucket API
  7. Native per-ecosystem registry APIs (pypi, npm, gem, cargo, maven, nuget, composer, golang proxy, hackage, hex, pub, cran, bioconductor HTML scrape + ecosyste.ms, conda)
  8. Go module proxy and forge Releases pages (timeline reconciliation fallback)
  9. Earlier-generation sources: OSSF Scorecard BigQuery dataset, GitHub dependency-graph GraphQL

Role of AI (as found, no speculation)

  • The tooling is AI-agent-BUILT: POC_stack README says code largely produced with code-gen tools; alpha_stack carries CLAUDE.md + agent-reproducible implementation plans.
  • The data generation itself is deterministic API probing/corroboration — no LLM calls in any pipeline code inspected.
