ADS access control today + improvements needed for feature-flag-gated datasets

Facts verified 2026-07-13 by reading anchore/enterprise-data-service-infra (lambdas), anchore/enterprise-data-service (publish workflows), and enterprise v5 (data_syncer, license machinery). Companion notes: [[b1ab40c9-86b]] (OSS Insights R&D), [[a39ac61b-1fa]] (Jira/software-index).

How access control works TODAY

Cloud side (enterprise-data-service-infra/v1): three request lambdas (get-listing-json, handle-dataset-request, handle-schema-list) + one authorizer. - Authorizer (authorization/app.py): regex-extracts Bearer v1_anc_{api_key}; NO validation of the key itself — it returns an API-GW policy with usageIdentifierKey=<api_key> and Allow on resource * (hardcoded). Actual key validity = API Gateway usage-plan lookup. Also emits EDS_API_USAGE_TRACKING log records (sha256 of key, anchorectl/enterprise versions, deployment UUID, source IP) -> CloudWatch subscription filter -> Firehose (per-key metrics; queried by ads-license-usage-query). - Dataset lambdas: hardcoded if/elif mapping of 6 dataset names (vulnerability_db, clamav_db, kev_db, epss_db, vulnerability_match_exclusions_db, stig_profiles_db) -> fixed S3 listing/prefix. Zero per-customer logic. Every valid key gets identical listings and archives (grype v6 on private GW returns a 1h pre-signed S3 URL). DEVELOPING.md's "listing files tailored for each customer" does NOT match the code — listings are per-dataset, not per-customer. - The lambda layer never sees the license. There is no dataset-level authorization decision anywhere in the cloud path: valid key = all datasets.

License format (enterprise common/license.py, license_model.py): signed YAML — details list (version, product, license{user/org/expiration/…}, entitlements[], support, data{apiKey, dataKey}) + RSA PKCS1-v1.5/SHA-256 signature over the canonical-JSON details, verified against a public key baked into enterprise. data.apiKey is the ADS API key. Entitlement vocabulary exists (LicenseEntitlement): Module:SBOM, Module:Secure, Module:Enforce, AddOn:PolicyPack:FedRamp, AddOn:PolicyPack:DoD, AddOn:Runtime:Kubernetes, AddOn:Runtime:ECS, AddOn:STIG:Static, AddOn:STIG:Runtime.

Enterprise-side enforcement (the only place flags are enforced): utils/feature_entitlements.py — Features enum -> FeatureMap -> CheckFeatureEntitlementLicense reads license.entitlements; decorator on API endpoints (400 when missing). data_syncer does NOT check entitlements: it shells anchorectl airgap feed download --key <license_key> and syncs everything the key can reach.

Proof of the gap: STIG profiles are an add-on (AddOn:STIG:*) yet stig_profiles_db is served by the lambda to ANY valid key and synced by every deployment; the flag only gates the enterprise API/UI. Add-on data enforcement today is honor-system client-side.

Improvements needed for feature-flag granularity in the lambda

  1. Get entitlements to the authorizer. The lambda only has the opaque api_key. Two viable designs: (a) server-side entitlement registry keyed by api_key (DynamoDB, populated by the license-issuance pipeline; authorizer looks up entitlements and passes them via authorizer context to backend lambdas); (b) client presents a signed entitlements claim (the license signature is RSA-verifiable in the lambda with just the public key — anchorectl already holds the full license). (a) enables revocation + changes without reissuing licenses; (b) is stateless. Hybrid: (b) for authenticity + (a) for revocation.
  2. Per-dataset authorization decision. Either scope the authorizer policy to entitled routes (caution: API GW caches authorizer responses per token — the cached policy must cover every route the token may hit, so per-resource statements need cache-aware design) or keep Allow-* and enforce per-dataset inside get-listing-json/handle-dataset-request using the entitlements passed in the authorizer context. The in-lambda check is simpler and cache-safe.
  3. Data-driven dataset registry with entitlement requirements. Replace the triplicated if/elif chains (3 lambdas x 6 datasets) with a shared registry: dataset name -> {s3 prefix, listing key, required_entitlement|None}. New datasets (oss_insights_db, eol_db) then ship with a required entitlement, e.g. AddOn:Insights:PackageEOL.
  4. Entitlement-filtered discovery. handle-schema-list currently returns the same static set to everyone; it should return only entitled datasets so clients auto-discover what they can sync (this is what makes new add-on datasets appear dynamically without client upgrades — Zach Hill's requirement on ENTERPRISE-6095).
  5. Client-side graceful degradation. anchorectl airgap feed download + data_syncer must treat per-dataset 403 as "not entitled, skip" (not sync failure), and pick up newly-entitled datasets on the next cycle after a license swap.
  6. Entitlement vocabulary extension. Add insight dataset entitlements to LicenseEntitlement + Features + FeatureMap so cloud-side and enterprise-side gating share names (per-dataset add-ons must be independently toggleable, and bundles combined atomically, per the 6095 SKU comment).
  7. Key lifecycle gaps (exists today, worse with paid add-on data): license expiry is enforced only inside enterprise (_license_validate_timestamps); the API-GW key does not expire with the license — an expired license's apiKey keeps fetching datasets until the key is manually removed from the usage plan. The issuance pipeline should sync key expiry/revocation into the registry from improvement 1.
  8. Usage-tracking per dataset. EDS_API_USAGE_TRACKING records identify the key but not the dataset requested; add dataset/route to the usage record so add-on data consumption can be measured (pricing/renewal signals).

Provisioning unknowns (not in these repos)

How data.apiKey values get registered as API-GW usage-plan keys (license-issuance tooling lives elsewhere — likely internal); whether dataKey (the second field in license data) is used anywhere in this path.

terminal:auto-0709-092918 · 2026-07-13 15:20 · open · 5c58c9d6-a5d Provisioning unknowns RESOLVED (2026-07-13): the license generator is anchore/anchore-lms (License Management System, JS web app, last pushed 2026-02). At license creation (src/services/post_license.js): IF 'Third_Party_Feeds' is in the chosen entitlements, LMS creates a fresh API Gateway API key (named by customer email + license id) via apigateway.createApiKey, embeds it as data.apiKey, sets data.dataKey to a STATIC shared constant (DATA_KEY — same for all customers), adds the key to ONE global usage plan (single USAGE_PLAN_ID), persists {license_id, api_key, api_key_id} in the LMS DB, then RSA-SHA256-signs JSON.stringify(details) with the private KEY_FILE and emits the YAML. So today's entitlement->ADS link is exactly one binary flag: Third_Party_Feeds = master switch for ALL datasets; no per-dataset anything. The UI offers the full entitlement menu (Third_Party_Feeds, Module:Secure/Enforce/SBOM, policy packs, etc.) but only Third_Party_Feeds affects ADS key issuance; deployment-type selection defaults entitlements to ['Third_Party_Feeds']. NO key revocation/disable/expiry sync exists anywhere in LMS — confirms improvement 7. Implication for the feature-flag plan: LMS is the natural writer of the entitlement registry (improvement 1) — it already knows api_key_id + entitlements at issuance and already has AWS API GW credentials; options are a DynamoDB registry write or tagging the API GW key with entitlements at createApiKey time.

terminal:auto-0709-092918 · 2026-07-13 15:59 · open · 6229bf37-e2e DESIGN DECISION (operator, 2026-07-13): stateless license-in-request, NOT a backend entitlement registry. Client (anchorectl) sends the full signed license with each request; the lambda validates the RSA signature with the baked-in public key and reads entitlements directly from the validated details. Rationale: no database synchronization problem, significantly less code/state; signature-validation + network cost of a few-KB license is insignificant. Supersedes improvement 1 option (a) — DynamoDB registry is OFF the table. Bonus: per-request expiry checking from the license timestamps fixes improvement 7 without key-lifecycle syncing. Agreed hardening details: (1) keep the API GW usage-plan key layered underneath as the mid-term revocation brake + rate limiting + usage metrics; (2) lambda must cross-check license.data.apiKey == presented bearer key to prevent pairing a leaked license with a different key; (3) license transported in custom header (b64) or body — mind authorizer identity-source size limits; prefer validating in the dataset lambdas rather than the authorizer to avoid cache-key complexity; (4) lambda trusts a LIST of public keys to allow signing-key rollover. Migration is backward-compatible: old clients that send only the key keep access to base datasets; flag-gated datasets require the license-bearing client.

Data Virtual Offsite (2026-07-16) — decisions & directives distilled from both transcripts

Attendees: Jeremy, Dan Nurmi (part 1 only), Zach Hill, Sherry (PM), Leon (part 2). Source: part1-transcript.txt (1h34m), part2-transcript.txt (1h33m), whisper distil-large-v3.

Scope decisions

  • DISTRO EOL IS CUT FROM THIS ANALYSIS ("lop off distro EOL"; focus package EOL). Different use case: different cardinality/APIs/schema/storage; joins at asset level not package rows; mixed-distro SBOMs possible (non-Syft); needs product input on surfacing. NOTE: distro EOL data already ships inside grype DB (endoflife.date via vunnel) — just not copied into Postgres; a quick image-centric legacy-side path exists but would be revisited under the new approach.
  • Risk score deferred from V1 (just another metadata key later; no architectural impact).
  • Phased releases explicitly OK: tranche 1 display-only → policy → search/reporting. Display alone yields coverage-feedback signal PM wants.
  • V1 metric selection: start NARROW on metrics, WIDE on package coverage; ideally one metric per category (boolean/time/qualitative/quantitative) to vet typed end-to-end consumption pre-production. Jeremy to hands-on the POC APIs and return a V1 dataset proposal (80/20 rule) + PM sign-off. "Once we decide the V1 dataset, everything downstream is obvious."
  • Qualitative metrics (popular/maintained): PM (Sherry) cautious for first release — categories stay, surface a subset.

Universe & collection

  • Universe generated backend-side, never from customer data. Seeds: vulnerability-known purls (FIRST tranche — sync with Weston/Josh on Waterville identifier overlap; avoid two identifier-generation approaches), GitHub repo listings, deps.dev, ecosyste.ms, ClearlyDefined, and Syft-generated SBOMs over public images (DockerHub/GHCR) — purls are invented strings, so harvesting Syft's own output aligns the dataset with customer SBOM purl dialect. Start with purl types Syft has catalogers for.
  • Identifiers are versionless (matching key); version/release data lives in insights records as information (not metrics).
  • oss-identifiers approach validated: probe iteration TO CONVERGENCE + evidence/agreement resolution + per-source canonical weighting; symmetry experiments become a QA/regression harness; two-phase minimum. deps.dev caveat (github.com/x/y always returns a Go record, 200) = why single-source is catastrophic.
  • Refresh cadence: per-metric/per-source (EOL slow; releases faster); days-weeks acceptable, not vuln-style hours; 7-day TTLs fine; publish to customers daily at most initially. Rate-limit reality: 3-4M projects/couple days possible; ecosyste.ms 5k/hr ≈ 117-day full pass; Maven effectively untraversable (years); npm CouchDB-style dumps exist (prior art at Anchore); deps.dev BigQuery bulk snapshot (~20TB) copyable into own GCP account — then their API is unnecessary.
  • Licensing of sources: ecosyste.ms + purldb share-alike acknowledged; legal review pending; agreement design degrades gracefully if a source is dropped (deps.dev-only mode was validated).
  • Stage persistence architecture confirmed: every stage persists output; corrections/overrides possible at each stage; per-record audit trail (evidence, timestamps, "EOL on date X because evidence Y").
  • Backend master data will be GBs→TBs (audit/metadata/cache); shipped sqlite stays small (records only).
  • Validators run inside the pipeline at each stage boundary (schema+property conformance, liveness probes — is the purl really on npmjs, does the URL resolve; possibly AI validators).
  • Compute: "weapons free with Amazon" — cloud-native managed services (SQS/Dynamo/BigTable/BigQuery ok), long-running stateful orchestration, serverless acceptable even at cost premium, NO EC2 pets, low care-and-feeding is a hard requirement; FastAPI for any web UI; internal tooling auth = existing SSO (IAM/Cognito/Okta/Cloudflare Access), NO custom auth; later read-only vs editor roles (security data).
  • Inspection/audit web dashboard: read-only first (status, per-stage throughput, record history/evidence); same screens later gain write = centralized corrections UI. SLA/monitoring/alerting is a line item.
  • Unknown-vs-default: NEVER default missing data (no data ≠ active). Known-unknowns explicit, possibly in the dataset itself (purl-seen-but-unknown; known-proprietary signal; maybe an unofficial purl namespace for proprietary). Operator: "revise that before we kick off generation."

Enterprise/platform decisions

  • Enterprise overrides/annotations committed ("100%"): two layers — centralized corrections (everyone) and deployment-local annotations/contextualization (like vuln annotations).
  • Generic join + generic insights surface: standardized join from component_catalog packages to insights; arbitrary key/value metadata flows through; ONE new generic policy gate keying off any insight key (e.g. package.insights.eol == true), not per-metric gates. Data-driven end to end.
  • API must ADVERTISE THE INSIGHTS SCHEMA (types/ranges/choices) so the UI renders columns/filters dynamically — policy-editor precedent (runtime-described gates). UI must not hard-bake insights.
  • API presence semantics: insights appear/disappear with entitlement — design for absence (empty vs separate endpoints; 403-consistent). UI mockups needed for unlicensed/no-data/missing states.
  • Diff detection on the insights table drives targeted policy re-eval (same pattern as vuln feed-update), same update workflow.
  • Search/reporting intersection (deferred but coming): insights must join package search ("all packages EOL in last 30 days across apps"); data-driven keys complicate query validation (talk w/ Ben Beauregard); JSONB fine for the record but INDEXABILITY for search must be designed in now.
  • Store the dataset UNPRUNED locally (no inventory-pruning optimization; keeps deltas simple); arbitrary- purl lookup becomes architecturally free (whether to expose = PM/RFE question).
  • No-upgrade data delivery confirmed as Neil's requirement: new insights datasets/SKUs (quarterly-ish cadence goal) consumable by already-deployed enterprise versions; richer workflows may require upgrade.

Delivery/ADS decisions

  • Ship as additional ADS feeds; invisible to non-consuming clients; core enterprise unaffected.
  • License work confirmed: RSA public key onto the lambda, verify license, enforce entitlements, dynamically enable feeds (matches the stateless license-in-request design).
  • PREVIEW/TEASER question (Neil): wants in-product upsell previews (e.g. 6.3 "insights preview — contact sales"); needs answer NOW because early- vs late-stage entitlement check changes delivery. No commercial restriction on distributing our own data (changes if data is ever purchased). Options: block at download; sync-but-feature-gate; or a separate teaser feed (same schema, top-N subset, own entitlement — no code changes). Trials are fully featured regardless.
  • SKU permutation question OPEN: one insights DB + enterprise-side entitlement filtering vs per-SKU datasets composed by ADS. Zach: SKUs iterate constantly (federal per-analyzer precedent) — keep license intelligence OUT of services; licensing loosely coupled to data delivery. Jeremy to recommend in days.
  • Decouple curation cycle from packaging cycle (snapshot-based publish; delivery format not baked into pipeline). V1 = full-dataset daily pulls (~1GB fine); design early for diffs/deltas (append-only friendly), hot/cold split, ecosystem slicing config (exclude ecosystems w/o customer data flowing up); same delta need incoming for grype DB v7. Air gap invariant: unidirectional; full dataset local; no interactive API.
  • ADS stability goal: adding datasets/metrics should NOT require touching ADS/distribution code.

Milestone 1 (agreed)

End-to-end POC of a productionable pipeline design publishing into the ADS dev AWS account, with TWO data pieces under separate entitlements to demo dynamism: load license → data appears through to UI; remove → disappears; zero code changes in the middle. "That's the vision."

Process/work-structure decisions

  • The binder = the planning/scoping view (validated: "these are the right blocks" — Zach; the two-box collection/dataset split = intermediate vs published state). Next: one FUNCTIONAL SPEC per component box ("practically pseudocode level"), each a living markdown driving agentic development, each with its own work breakdown; multi-repo topology needs a top-level home linking subproject specs.
  • Jira: lean doc-driven — point a big epic/story at the spec rather than exploding ~100 4-hour sub-tasks; human-reviewable structure and kept-current module docs are mandatory (Leon).
  • Sequencing: understanding before scheduling; timeline discussion next week; Jeremy first: hands-on the data-source APIs, then V1 dataset proposal + entitlement-delivery recommendation.
  • Effort estimate (Jeremy): 80/20 — pipeline is the work and ALL the risk (external services, rate limits); platform consumption is mechanically simple.
